## D155 — A seat that cannot run a command is not a delivery channel: refuse the start, attribute the provider before asking for money, and stop crediting instruments git has never seen (2026-10-28, delegate; measurement + operating decision, no operator ruling taken)

**What was decided, and why the *why* matters.** Three rules came out of one session that set out to answer "what
happens if I start the channel now?".

**1. Channel readiness is measured at the seat's *hands*, not at the broker's liveness.** `tools/broker-serve.mjs
--dry-run` and `tools/channel-preflight.mjs` now refuse with **`seat-shell-availability`** (ROADMAP 217's own
acceptance asked for this block) because the seat tool set registers `powershell`, the pinned build tries
`["pwsh","powershell"]` and re-throws the last spawn error
(`vendor/pi-main/packages/durable/src/tools/bash.ts:169`), and **neither exists on this Linux box**. *Why this is a
ruling and not a bug note:* the constitution's oracle is "`node demo/<name>.test.mjs` … exit 0 is a pass", and the
completion rule tells a seat to run the checks that exercise its item. With no spawnable shell a seat can still edit
files, so it can still *produce* work it cannot *prove* — every completion becomes self-declared. A wake that cannot
run the oracle is worse than no wake, because it manufactures green claims. The store proves it already fired, not
merely that it could: `spawn powershell ENOENT` ×3 + `spawn pwsh ENOENT` ×1, newest `entry #274074`
(`2026-10-28T17:09:07.533Z`, conv 4930 = **devtools**, the seat that owns #726) — **inside the last broker pass**,
0.2 s before that pass' last provider call.

**2. Attribute a provider error to an era before recommending money (ROADMAP 226/229).** `channel-preflight` §5's naive
read of the last 30 submission rows prints `402 "You need positive balance" ×5`, which invites the operator to fund an
account that is no longer in use. Attributed properly it is history: `attempts local/iq3_s=14, deepinfra/…=8,
unattributed=8`, and **every failure belongs to the `deepinfra` era; the live `local/iq3_s` era has none** (the 14,377
`402` generations predate the 2026-10-27T04:55Z move to local). *The join shape is the finding:* a submission row
carries no admission age (**229**), and its `entry` is the **admitted input** entry — it has a timestamp but no
`model[0]`. The provider/model that ran the turn lives on the **first assistant entry after it** in that conversation
(`select record from entries where conversation_id = ? and id > ? order by id limit 40`). Joining to the admitted entry
itself yields a timestamp and a **null provider**, which silently reads as "unattributed".

**3. An untracked instrument is an uncreditable instrument (new ROADMAP 233).** Eight files this session read or ran —
`tools/worktree-cleanup.mjs`, `src/worktree-cleanup.mjs`, and six `demo/` members (`worktree-cleanup`, `broker-serve`,
`clock-skew`, `broker-clock-step`, `verify-sweep-cleanup`, `verify-sweep-adversarial`, all `.test.mjs`) — are now absent
from disk **and from `git ls-files`**; `git log --all --diff-filter=A` for those paths prints nothing, so `git status`
cannot show the loss and history cannot restore it. Two ROADMAP rows credit two of them as landed, and 217's acceptance
names a test file that no longer exists to extend. `scripts/suite.mjs:36` enumerates with `readdirSync(demoDir)`, so a
deleted member is a **silent shrink, not a failure**. **Rule adopted: "landed" requires `git ls-files` membership** —
a delegate may not credit an instrument it cannot `git show`, and a delegate's own durable evidence goes to a tracked
path (`docs/incidents/…`), not only to gitignored `.spike/`.

**4. "Self-healing" a worktree ledger is data loss on a moved workspace (new ROADMAP 232).** `pruneWorktrees`
(`src/worktree.mjs:649`) runs `git -C <repo> worktree prune`, which deletes every registration whose directory this host
cannot read; it is called **unconditionally** at the end of the broker sweep (`src/broker.mjs:1167`, whose comment says
"…whether or not it removed anything this pass") and after every removal (`src/worktree.mjs:667`, `:1326`). Measured
inside one session that ran no writing verb on the workspace: the main checkout's ledger went **36 registrations (20 of
them `C:\Users\Alex\…`) → 1**, `.git/worktrees` empty. The same end state is recorded at
`docs/incidents/2026-10-26-worktree-and-scratch-sweep.md:20-30`, so this is the third recording of one class, and the
runbook's own Step-1 command (`node tools/worktree-cleanup.mjs --dry-run`) is now `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. The fix is a
**scoping grant**, not the removal of pruning — ghost registrations were a real problem the prune solved (25 cleared on
2026-10-19).

**Cost, stated so the next session does not re-derive it.** Preflight **2.0 → 3.3 s**; the whole delta is the store
evidence, and it is **one** `entries` scan carrying all six `LIKE` patterns as aliased aggregates
(`sum(record like '%…%') a0, … e5`) at ~0.9 s — six separate scans cost ~1.9 s on 137,427 rows. `broker-serve --dry-run`
**2.93 s** (was 2.79 s), `--status` **2.75 s** (unchanged): importing `src/seattools.mjs` to read the *real* tool set
rather than re-deriving it is free at that resolution.

**What I deliberately did not decide.** No channel start, no `up`/`worktree`/`run`/`send`/`resume`/`doctor` — **no
writing verb on this workspace**; no ledger surgery; no queue transition; no intent spooled; no push; no edit of the
operator-owned `rig.selfdev.json` (the seat-instruction sentence that names "powershell" is theirs to change). The
sweep's mechanism for the **file** losses is **named as a candidate, not proven**, and I did not "fix" it by hand —
ROADMAP 212's acceptance (byte-identical pre-existing tree) is the instrument that would prove it, and it is still
unimplemented.

## D156 — The pre-move Windows volume is the authority for cross-OS evidence; `.git/worktrees` and untracked files are caches, so durability means `git ls-files`, and a rehearsal never runs on the working checkout (2026-10-28, operator ruling on the delegate's asks; executed by the delegate)

**The ruling.** Asked four things — restore the pre-move refs from the other NVMe volume, spool the routing fact to `pm`,
stage the channel rehearsal in a disposable clone instead of starting from the main checkout, and turn "untracked is
uncreditable" into a running check — the operator agreed to all four and **held the clock item** pending an explanation of
what it buys. The channel itself stays withheld on ROADMAP **217**. The delegate executed the ref restore, the rehearsal
clone and the check, and did **not** touch `src/`, `demo/` or `scripts/`.

**Why, and with what evidence.** The ledger collapse and the instrument loss in
`docs/incidents/2026-10-28-cross-os-ledger-pruned-and-untracked-loss.md` share one cause: both trusted a **cache** as if it
were an archive. `.git/worktrees` is regenerated by `git worktree prune` and `pruneWorktrees` (`src/worktree.mjs:649`,
called unconditionally at `src/broker.mjs:1167`) will clear any registration this host cannot read — including a
`C:\Users\…` registration that is the *only* record of what a cross-OS workspace pointed at. An untracked file is the same
kind of cache: `scripts/suite.mjs:36` enumerates members from disk, so a deleted member is a silently smaller suite, and
`git log --all --diff-filter=A` proves the eight lost instruments were never in git, so nothing could be restored.
Measured against the pre-move volume: **0** Oct-24-era files are absent here, and after the event this checkout has **0**
untracked files under `demo tools src scripts` — so what was lost was exactly the untracked set. Conversely **23 of the 30**
queue-cited shas that resolved nowhere resolve after copying the Windows clone's three `*.pack` files (13,057 objects this
clone lacked; `git fsck --connectivity-only` clean; 467 commits reachable from no ref), which is the same evidence class the
runbooks call protected. Therefore: **durability means `git ls-files` membership, nothing less**, and cross-OS evidence is
read from the pre-move volume into a **committed** file, never left in `.spike/` or in a cache directory.

**Operating consequence (binding on the delegate).** (1) A rehearsal, a sweep, or any worktree-exercising test run happens
in a **disposable clone** — `/home/chexxor/Git/Durian-Pi-ops`, with its own store copy — not in the working checkout; that
is what let `broker-serve --dry-run` be proven to refuse on `seat-shell-availability` while both ledgers stayed at 1 row.
(2) A delegate instrument that a ROADMAP row credits must be **committed in the same item that credits it** (214's commit
boundary), and `tools/instrument-provenance.mjs` is the tripwire that makes an untracked or missing instrument loud
(46 ms; `suite members: git=238 disk=238`; exits 1 on membership or ledger drift). (3) Recovered pre-move objects are
**perishable**: a `git gc --prune=now` on either side destroys the 467 unreachable commits for good, so importing them is
an operator grant the delegate asked for rather than assumed — the copy was rehearsed in the disposable clone and **not**
applied to the working checkout. (4) Re-created instruments are labelled **re-created**, never "restored".

**What was deliberately not done.** No pack copy into the working checkout (awaiting the grant; the numbers above are the
rehearsal's), no `git worktree prune`/`remove` anywhere, no queue transition, no `rig.selfdev.json` edit (the drafted
`bash` sentence is recorded in ROADMAP 217 instead), no `set-local-rtc` (the operator held the clock item), and no push.

## D157 — The delegate may act inside the project; nothing that changes the host operating system is delegated, and the pre-move object import is granted but bounded (2026-10-28, operator ruling)

**The ruling.** Asked to act on the recommended actions and whether the clock change is host-wide, the operator granted the
actions and set the boundary: **a change is approvable at delegate level only if it applies to this project/workspace**.
`timedatectl set-local-rtc 0` is host-wide, so it stays unapplied and un-delegated.

**Applied under the grant (working checkout, additive, reversible).** The pre-move Windows clone's **three `*.pack` files**
were copied into `/home/chexxor/Git/Durian-Pi/.git/objects/pack/` and `git index-pack` run on each: object count
**9,301 → 22,351**, `git fsck --connectivity-only` reports no corruption (dangling objects only), **2,083 commit objects
against 1,628 reachable from refs — 455 commits exist only as unreachable objects**, and **23 of the 30** queue-cited shas
that resolved nowhere now resolve here (the 6 that resolve in neither clone stay listed in the incident). `git worktree
list` stayed at **1 registration** before and after. Only `*.pack` files were copied; copying a pack's
`.idx/.rev/.mtimes/multi-pack-index` was measured to break every object read with `fatal: mmap failed: Permission denied`.

**Why the boundary is right, not timid.** The clock item is not a preference: `LocalRTC=yes` with the RTC holding CDT is a
**5 h** mislabel (`RTCTimeUSec=Wed 2026-10-28 16:02:43 UTC` while UTC was `20:02:43Z`), and a 42 m 42 s backward step
already happened inside one session — but the fix rewrites the OS's reading of the hardware clock for **every** process and
changes what Windows displays at the next boot. The project-scoped half of the same problem is real and is now routed as
ROADMAP **234**: the rig's budgets are wall-clock arithmetic (`heartbeat 60 s`, `stranded-admitted 30 s`, `admission
5 min`, `genlock reservation 11 min`) while the store's own stamps are **relative** (`documents.created_at` spans
`1 … 2,263,478`; `entries` has no wall-clock column), so the rig cannot see a step happen. `tools/channel-preflight.mjs`
§8 is the delegate-side tripwire: it prints the host clock posture and a wall-vs-monotonic delta (~60 ms of a 3.33 s run)
and **never** applies a fix.

**Still perishable, still the operator's call.** Those 455 unreachable commits are anchored by nothing; a
`git gc --prune=now` on either side destroys them for good. Anchoring them (e.g. `refs/rescued/orphan-*` per sha) is a
repo-shape change the delegate did **not** make unasked.
## D158 — Agent-authored harness customization ships as an installable package developed in the workspace, not as hand-written `.pi/` files; and 232 is gated on a read of shipped enforcement designs before any build (2026-10-28, operator ruling)

**The ruling.** Asked for three rulings (a `.pi/` grant for ROADMAP 235/236/238; whether to register the
capture-on-success item; whether 232 stays first), the operator ruled: **"You can write into the .pi directory if
necessary. It would be ideal if we did not have to do that, but use existing mechanisms such as custom extension
installation, which we could develop in this workspace."** Registration of capture-on-success: *"2. is fine."* On 232:
**"Do more research before proceeding onto roadmap 232."** The clone grant came separately the same day: *"Please do the
git cloning, depth 1, for us."*

**Why the package shape is a substance call, not a tidiness call.** pi's package mechanism already gives the
project-scoped surface with a smaller trust footprint than hand-written config: `pi install ./local-package` loads a
**local path in place, without copying**, `--local` writes the declaration into `.pi/settings.json`, and "Pi reads
declarations from that file only after project trust is granted"
(`@1.4.0 docs/packages.md`, "Install and manage packages" / "Choose a source"). So the repo-committed object is a
**directory of code plus one settings line**, both in `git ls-files`, both diffable, both reinstallable on the other
host — instead of agent-authored `.mjs` sitting loose in the directory that *is* the trust decision. That difference is
exactly what round 2 of this study says nobody solves: **no vendor distributes per-project instructions across two
hosts**, and symlinks "work only if Windows Developer Mode is enabled"
(`docs/reviews/harness-tools-skills-public-harnesses-research.md` §3.7). A package that lives in the tree and is
installed by a one-line declaration is the only shape in this study that survives a host move.

**What it changes in the register.** 235's *Where:* no longer names a hand-written
`.pi/extensions/delegate-instruments.mjs`; it names a package in this tree (e.g. `packages/delegate-instruments/`) with
conventional `extensions/` (+ optional `skills/`, `prompts/`) directories, installed `--local`. `.pi/extensions/` stays
the fallback if the package path hits a wall, and `pi -e ./path` stays the no-write trial mode (`docs/usage.md` "Load
extensions and packages from paths or packages"). 240 (capture-on-success) and **241** (research-before-232) were
registered with reasons; **242** and **243** were registered from defects measured during this work, not from the
operator's asks.

**Evidence for the execution of the grant.** Five `--depth 1` clones landed under `vendor/eval/`: `codex d373d649`
(139 M, full Rust source), `cline 51f63e4f` (122 M), `goose 775b3958` (647 M), `claude-code-docs 58d6da1e` (31 M,
**CHANGELOG/docs only — no implementation**), `copilot-cli 84ee80ea` (596 K, **README/`install.sh`/changelog only** —
the CLI is closed, so its value is its issue tracker). `node tools/vendor-pins.mjs --write docs/VENDOR-PINS.md --tags`
then `--check` → **PIN CHECK PASS (14 clones)**; `git worktree list --porcelain` stayed at **1 registration** before and
after the clones. Live-page confirmation of the report's load-bearing numbers, same day: Claude Code's "1% of the model's
context window", "truncated at 1,536 characters", "first 5,000 tokens of each" / "combined budget of 25,000 tokens",
`/skill-doctor`, `/run-skill-generator`; Codex `config-advanced`'s `project_doc_max_bytes`,
`thread.skills.truncated`, `skill.injected`, `history.jsonl`, `hooks.json`, `PreToolUse`; Cursor's `beforeShellExecution`,
`failClosed`, `pluginPaths`.

**What did NOT change.** 232 is still unclaimed and untouched — no suite runs from this checkout (the 15-minute
self-sweep, `docs/incidents/2026-10-29-windows-vm-suite-self-sweep.md`). The delegate still does not claim, complete or
route queue items: 240-243 are **registered-not-scheduled**, and pm owns ordering. The `.pi/` grant is real but
**unused** so far — no `.pi/` path exists in this tree.
## D159 — The research agent is off-host with no repo write access: the delegate is the landing path, and a citation's portable unit is a quote, not a line range (2026-10-28, operator statement; runbook amended by the delegate)

**The constraint, stated by the operator.** *"The research agent is not on this computer, and does not have write access to
the repo."* That invalidates two things already written down: the round-3 prompt asked the agent to `git add` its deliverable
and to ship an `inputs/fetched/` corpus, and `docs/runbooks/research-request.md` asked for *"the deliverable path"* without
ever saying **who moves the artifact into the repo**. Round 2 is what that omission costs: the report arrived citing
`[^542f21#49]`-style line ranges into pages fetched into the agent's **own** workspace — 64 distinct in-body markers, 14
defined, **50 unopenable from this repo**, plus 3 vendor URLs now HTTP 404.

**Why this changes the prompt's shape, not just its last step.** A line range is an address into *a copy someone else has*.
With no file channel, the only citation unit that survives the trip is **a verbatim quote of ≤ 40 words + the URL + the
agent's own fetch date**: the delegate can fetch that page itself, on a later date, and still find the sentence. Asking for
line ranges instead manufactures checkability that no one downstream can exercise — and the delegate's own copies are dated
**2026-10-28**, later than the agent's read, so even a correct range may no longer point where it did. The rule is therefore:
quote required, line range welcome **beside** it, and **a quote the delegate cannot locate is recorded `unverified` in the
folded docs while the agent's report body stays verbatim** — we correct our record, not their artifact.

**Changed today.** `docs/runbooks/research-request.md`: Preconditions (the constraint; prompts ask for *content to copy*,
never for commits or repo writes), Do 1 (Deliverable gains the copy-paste shape — one fenced block per section, no narration,
because round 2's arrival had the agent's working notes glued to the title line; Evidence discipline gains the
quote-portability rule), Do 5 (the delegate commits **on the agent's behalf**, and fetches + manifests + quote-checks first),
Verify (citation integrity is **measured**: marker-vs-definition count and an HTTP check of every evidence URL), and "If it
fails" now names four failure modes with their handling. `inputs/fetched/README.md` states who fetches and why, the manifest
columns including *quotes found in this copy*, and the `grep` that is the verification step. Round-3 prompt
`docs/reviews/harness-tools-skills-followup-2-research-prompt.md` rewritten accordingly: Task A2 asks for quotes and states
"you cannot send us files"; "What not to do" now forbids file writes, clones and commits outright.

**What did NOT change.** The delegate still cannot call the research agent (routing stays the operator's,
`docs/runbooks/research-request.md` "Escalate to"). The agent still owns the questions — the delegate taking over the
*fetching* is plumbing, not the delegate answering research by guessing. And ROADMAP **240–243** remain
registered-not-scheduled: pm sequences them.
**Addendum the same day — the rule has a second half, learned from the delegate's own error.** Quotes are only half of
citation integrity; the other half is **pointers**. While repairing round 2's evidence chain the delegate found that **it had
mis-attributed and then propagated** two GitHub issue numbers across three files (`docs/COMPETITORS.md`, ROADMAP **241**, two
review notes): it cited `copilot-cli` #978/#4438 for *fail-open hooks* behaviour, but those issues exist and the report cites
them **correctly for its skills claims** ("Skills are not used unless explicitely stated"; "`disable-model-invocation: true`
makes a skill unreachable, not manual-only"). The report's own hooks rows sit on an **undefined** anchor; the report was more
sound than the delegate's fold. **The rule now: fetch the cited pointer and read its title before repeating a claim.** The payoff
was immediate — doing it surfaced better evidence than the report had, all title-checked 2026-10-28 and pinned in
`inputs/fetched/MANIFEST.md` §3: **#2893** *"preToolUse hooks silently bypassed under parallel tool calls (timeout->allow
fallback + serial dispatch…)"*, **#3590** *"PreToolUse hook `permissionDecision: "ask"` auto-approved by TUI since v1.0.53"*,
**#2540** *"Plugin-defined preToolUse hooks (hooks.json) do not fire — neither in main session nor subagents"*, **#5098**
*"sessionStart hook stops running after adding `sandbox.userPolicy.filesystem` paths"*. Read together they say something this
rig needs: **which plane a guard is declared on, and what config is present, decides whether it runs at all** — so an installed
guard that never fires is indistinguishable from a working one, which is why ROADMAP **235**'s package should ship a
`guard-status` instrument and ROADMAP **238**'s guard must be self-attesting. **A reachable URL is not a citation; a wrong
pointer is worse than no pointer, because it reads as verified.**

**Second amendment, same day — round 3 tested the rule, and the rule held (plus a ruling the delegate must not re-litigate).**
The research agent returned 60 numbered citations, each a URL + fetch date + ≤40-word quote, and **no files**; the delegate
re-fetched every page and grepped every quote in its own copies: **91 of 94 fragments located** (14/14 issue-body quotes, all
URLs 200). That is the evidence chain working, and it is now the template in `docs/runbooks/research-request.md`. Three things
this bought, in order of value: (1) **it caught the delegate's own claims again** — a file size asserted from a working summary
(**1,457** lines claimed, **680** measured), a claim that `docs/COMPETITORS.md` carried a "goose is guard-less" row when **no
such row exists**, and a Goose `checks/*.sh` mechanism inherited from a summary that appears in **neither the deliverable nor
the pin** — so it was **not registered**, and ROADMAP **240**'s success-predicate question stays open. The general form, which is
what to remember: **a claim about a document is a claim about a file; run the command that reads the file before repeating it —
including when the source of the claim is your own session summary.** (2) It **displaced a bad design instinct with a shipped
one**: Codex keeps guard trust as `HookStateToml { enabled, trusted_hash, trusted_content_hash }` readable **only from the
`User`/`SessionFlags` layers** — "Project, managed, and plugin layers can discover hooks, but they do not get to write user hook
state" (`codex · d373d649 · hooks/src/config_rules.rs:8-14,24-30`) — which is exactly the split the rig needs between *the repo
carries the instrument* (D158) and *the repo cannot bless it*; registered as ROADMAP **245**, with **246** for the per-decision
record. (3) It killed a tidy conclusion: "four of five shipped guards fail open" is wrong — direction is **per event and per
version**, and Copilot CLI's same hook flipped direction between v1.0.18 and v1.0.57 (#2540). **Also recorded here as a ruling:
the operator released the phantom citation — "Forget about the phantom citation."** `docs/incidents/2026-10-29-windows-vm-suite-self-sweep.md`
stays missing; the recovery ask is withdrawn and no session should spend effort on it unless the operator reopens the question.
The date/timezone half of ROADMAP **244** and its cited-path check remain live.

## D160 — a research prompt must be *self-contained*: the round-4 sandbox held no copy of this repo, so every `docs/` path in the prompt was unreadable, and an unverified artifact gets tracked the session it lands

**Measured** (delegate, 2026-10-29T03:4xZ = 2026-10-28 22:4x host-local CDT, `Alex-Desktop-Win10`):
`docs/reviews/harness-tools-skills-public-harnesses-research-4.md` (17,412 B / 196 lines, sha256 `8e028729…`) opens
**"Status: I could not execute this as specified"** — *"The prompt file is not in this sandbox. `docs/` does not exist here."*
It therefore answered **reconstructed** questions, could not write, and could not produce response headers or `sha256sum`
output, refusing to fill the MANIFEST columns: *"A MANIFEST with those columns filled would be fabricated. Don't accept one."*
**Why this is a decision and not just an incident:** D159 already ruled that the research agent is off-host and the delegate is
the landing path, but it did not draw the consequence — if the agent cannot read the rig, **a prompt that points at `docs/` paths
is a prompt the agent cannot execute**, and the round costs the round-trip anyway. So: *(1)* prompts carry the questions and the
cited text inline, and name only paths as *descriptions of this repo*, never as things to open; *(2)* the byte-level evidence
columns (HTTP status, sha256, `Last-Modified`) are **delegate-obtained only**, by a native re-fetch — that is where 244's rule
about hashes already lives, and asking the researcher for them invites fabrication; *(3)* registered as ROADMAP **249** for the
runbook edit.

**Second half of the ruling (delegate practice, not an operator grant):** when a research artifact appears in the working tree,
**track it verbatim and unverified in the same session**, in its own commit that adopts no claim from it. *Why:* ROADMAP **233**
measured that untracked files this session reads are gone tomorrow, and D159 makes the artifact **non-regenerable** — the agent
that produced it cannot re-run on demand. The cost of tracking it early is one commit of unverified text; the cost of waiting is
that the evidence disappears, which is exactly what 243 recorded. Verification stays a separate commit, and the pointer says which
claims are still unverified. *(Naming hazard recorded under 244(iv): the series is named four ways — round 2 has no version
suffix, round 3 is `-r3.md`, round 4 is `-research-4.md`, and the prompt named `followup-2` is the round-3 prompt; a "round N"
prose reference is ambiguous until it is quoted as a path.)*

## D161 — a research round's citation block is never merged as text: land a key-alias table first, and re-anchor at the pin, not at the URL

**Delegate practice, not an operator grant** (delegate session 2026-10-29, Linux, `label-withheld-per-D205`; evidence in
`docs/reviews/harness-r4-verification-2026-10-29.md` and `inputs/fetched/MANIFEST.md` §4). Registered as ROADMAP **250**.

**Measured first.** The *integrated* report, `docs/reviews/harness-tools-skills-public-harnesses-research.md`, carries
**184** marker occurrences over **23** base keys and defines only **14** of them (its References block, lines 250–263) —
so **9 keys are dangling** (`542f21 b736c3 20106b d32e06 04a0b7 5389e9 3d9c8f 5f6188 dccefb`) while carrying sentences
`docs/ROADMAP.md` already relies on. Round 4's Task A names a source for 6 of the 9 — and **re-uses `[^1]` and `[^2]` for
different pages than round 2 does** (round 2: `[^1]` = the Claude Code hooks reference, `[^2]` = its skills page; round 4:
`[^1]` = skills, `[^2]` = Cursor rules) while also re-keying the same pages as hex tags. A paste in that direction does
not fail: it **silently re-points citations that already have downstream consumers**. Separately, re-fetching two cited
pages reproduced their recorded sha256 **exactly** (`bfde51ac…`, `ca7dc20c…`) while the Cline locator had rotted
(`docs.cline.bot/features/…` → `/customization/…`), and the "closed issue" claim that would have been pasted from round 4
is **false** (`github/copilot-cli#978` is open, `state_reason: reopened`).

**The ruling, and why.** (1) **Alias table before merge.** One table mapping `hex tag → existing key → URL at the
`inputs/fetched/MANIFEST.md` pin`, committed *before* any anchor is merged, and merging runs only old-keys → new-round,
never the reverse. *Why:* key namespaces in these reports are unowned — that is what produced the 9 dangling keys, and
the collision is invisible to a reader because both styles render identically. (2) **Re-anchor at the pin, not by
re-fetch.** For any vendor in `docs/VENDOR-PINS.md`, resolve the claim by reading the clone at its pinned HEAD; a web
page is for web-only vendors, and there only ≤40-word quotes travel (D159). *Why:* line anchors survive neither a
re-render nor a redirect, and this session proved the strongest form locally — `vendor/eval/cline@51f63e4
docs/customization/cline-rules.mdx` (398 lines) never mentions "Memory Bank", so round 2's `[^d32e06#79]` is page chrome,
a finding **no** re-fetch of the page can establish. (3) **A cited GitHub issue carries four API fields** — `state`,
`state_reason`, `reactions.total_count`, `comments`, read from `api.github.com` — because the issue *page* is unpinned
and mutable. *Why:* that one call is what caught a false correction in the report this gate existed to police, and it
cost ~3 s against a round that cost a session.

## D162 — citation integrity is a machine check, not a reading habit: family = filename stem, a URL verdict must name its evidence class, and the gate fails only on anchors that are wrong *today* (2026-10-29, delegate; instrument design + measurement, no operator ruling taken)

`tools/review-cite-check.mjs` (774 lines, zero deps, `--self-test` 12/12) plus the alias table
`docs/reviews/harness-citation-registry.md` (29 rows) now check the claims ROADMAP 250/244/243 registered. Over 127
files in `docs/reviews/`, `docs/incidents/`, `inputs/fetched/`: **524 findings, 292 hard, 81 files clean** —
148 dangling keys (89 hard), **108 key collisions**, **71 duplicate definitions**, 9 path citations no branch ever had,
2 elided addresses, 2 anchors past EOF at a pin, 6 size claims false at a pin, 5 dead URLs. Evidence and every command:
`docs/reviews/citation-integrity-corpus-2026-10-29.md`; the corpus item is **ROADMAP 252**.

**The rulings, and why.**

1. **An address is machine-checked or it is a rumor.** *Why:* `building-agent-systems-on-pi-research.md` defines
   `[^1]` at lines **111, 553, 987** with three targets, so **two of the three are unreachable no matter which
   tie-break a renderer picks** — and the vendored `marked` **18.0.11** (a transitive dependency; nothing in `src/`
   imports it, so this says nothing about our UI) resolves duplicates to the **first** and has **no footnote support at
   all**, rendering `[^1]: [Name](url)` as `<a href="%5BName%5D(url)">^1</a>`. A reader cannot see the defect, so a
   reader cannot fix it; the check is the only thing that makes the corpus repairable.
2. **A citation "family" is a shared filename stem, never mere cross-citation.** *Why:* inferring the namespace from
   who-cites-whom merged 22 unrelated reports and printed **81 fake collisions** around the 3 real ones. Ordinary
   Markdown gives every file its own footnote namespace; a checker that cries wolf is deleted within a session, and the
   whole point of 240–243 is that unread evidence is how phantom citations survived.
3. **A URL verdict must name its evidence class: 404/410/510 = dead; 401/403/429/503 = bot-blocked (soft); 3xx =
   rotted locator at a live page (soft, record the final URL in `inputs/fetched/MANIFEST.md` §6); network failure =
   unprobed, never dead.** *Why:* over **192** cited URLs, 9×403 + 4×429 + 1×401 were all **live** pages, and `curl`
   **without `-L`** returns **308** for `docs.cline.bot/features/cline-rules` and `cursor.com/docs/context/rules`, which
   are alive at moved addresses. The naive "does it resolve?" probe this replaces would have deleted live evidence and
   kept dead evidence — the Goose paths round 2 cites as `[^4] [^9] [^10]` are 404 **with no redirect** and are still
   cited in its §2 matrix.
4. **A fence is an example, a correction is not a bad claim, and a missing trailing newline is not a lie.** *Why:* the
   checker charged its own evidence note for the duplicate definition it was *illustrating* inside a ``` block, scored
   "680 lines, not the 1,457 from memory" as a defect, and called a 128-content-line file 127 because `wc -l` counts
   newlines. Failing corrections and examples trains readers to ignore the gate — the exact failure mode 240–243 exist
   to prevent. So: footnote syntax is skipped inside fences (paths, sizes, URLs still count there), corrections are
   `SIZE CLAIM CORRECTED IN LINE` soft, and off-by-one explained by a missing newline is soft.
5. **Two postures, deliberately different sets.** Full audit = every hard finding (the review queue). `--gate` = the
   **wrong-today** set only: collisions, duplicate definitions, phantom/malformed paths, anchors past EOF, pin drift,
   dead URLs, size claims at a pin — **203 of 524**, leaving the 89 hard dangling keys for the audit. *Why:* a gate that
   fires on 292 findings on day one is a gate nobody runs; a gate that fires on the 203 that are provably wrong now is a
   gate a doc-only change can be held to.
6. **Suppression is counted, never silent** — `<!-- cite-ns: quoted -->`, `<!-- cite-check: ignore-line -->`,
   `ignore-file`; the run prints `2 SUPPRESSED by cite-check markers`. *Why:* the runbook rule that a documented escape
   hatch beats the exception someone adds under pressure. The same run keeps `ALIAS INFERRED — NEEDS URL (8)` failing-
   visible every time, because 8 of the 15 registry aliases have a page name and no URL.
7. **The delegate fixed no report prose.** *Why:* re-keying rounds 3 and 4 onto round 2's numbers is the merge decision
   `pm` and a seat own (D161); the delegate's deliverable is the instrument, the registry, MANIFEST §6 and the evidence.
   Half-grammar — the repair is now *unowned queue work*, not an unknown: **0 queue rows** name 250/244/243/252.

## D163 — The verifier moves to a second served model, and `done` stops meaning "the author says so" (2026-10-29, operator rulings; executed by the delegate)

**What the operator ruled, in one session.** (1) The verifier seats go onto the secondary model server
(LM Studio at `http://127.0.0.1:1234`) **before** the team starts. (2) Every work item is **reviewed and merged to
`main` before the item is completed** — a process requirement, registered as **ROADMAP 253**. (3) The delegate may
**operate the model server**: unload a model, load another, and change load configurations, provided both models
can be served if they fit.

**Why the first ruling was not the small one it looked like.** The rig has been running **one model for all twelve
seats**: `check` reports `single-model-rig` **fix-now** — "all 12 seats resolve to `local/iq3_s`, so a shared blind
spot is systemic" — which means the author/verifier family invariant `SELFDEV.md` describes has been **false for
the whole period since the Linux move**, and `verification-without-evidence` is red on **435** items. So the flip is
not a tuning change; it restores a property the rig claims to have. And the seat count is **5, not 3**: calling the
product's own predicate (`src/verifierrole.mjs`, `seatsAreVerifier(seat)` — one seat object, not two strings) against
`rig.selfdev.json` matches `qa`, `qa2`, `auditor`, **`advocate`** and **`designer`**, because VERIFIER_TERMS includes
`"review"` and those two roles say "design reviewer" / "UX reviewer". `docs/SELFDEV.md` names only three, which is a
docs defect the scribe owns, not a delegate edit.

**Why the flip is staged rather than started.** `D137` binds: *"a verifier that fails the seeded-bug gate is worse
than no verifier"*, because clearing `single-model-rig` is only a **string comparison** (`src/checkup.mjs`), and a
verifier that invents a confident wrong mechanism injects false verdicts rather than removing blind spots. So the
rig/config change landed, and the **start** is gated on `tools/model-probes/gate.mjs --replicate 3` against flint,
which was still running at clock-out (`~2 min` per cell on a reasoning-heavy model). If flint fails the gate, the
answer is a remote cross-family verifier — **not** a return to the previous state: that model (`ministral-3-14b-reasoning`)
scored **0/2** (`D137`) and its loaded window was **8,192**, below every verifier seat's median prompt.

**The measurement that sets the window, and it is not a preference.** Over **60,503** `pi.assistant` turns in this
store (`input + cacheRead` joined to seats by conversationId): `qa` p50 **55,538** / p95 251,311 · `advocate` p50
**108,435** · `designer` p50 **66,258** · `auditor` p95 329,252 · `qa2` p95 48,640; **37,348** of the 60,503 exceed
32,768. A verifier window under ~55k guarantees compaction; 65,536 is a **floor**, and the durable fix is the
prompt-size work (**208**, the context-fraction guard), not an ever-larger window. `DURIG_VERIFIER_CONTEXT` was
declaring **13,273** while the server had that model loaded at **8,192** — the rig has been stating a window it was
not being given, and `DURIG_VERIFIER_MAX_TOKENS=32768` (raised in `D136` to survive a truncation artifact) was
larger than the whole declared window; it is now **8192** so 57,344 tokens of the 65,536 remain for the prompt.

**What was done to the server, and the trap that made it necessary.** LM Studio reported flint **loaded** at
`context_length: 262144` while every inference call returned `Failed to load model` — a *zombie instance*: the
listing is a registration, not a health check. Unloading and reloading with a **flat** body
(`context_length: 65536`, `flash_attention`, `offload_kv_cache_to_gpu`) fixed servability in **18.3 s**, and
unloading ministral freed **~12.7 GB** of the 3090; flint decodes **9.8 tok/s**, prefills COLD ~**212 tok/s**, and
**WARM** at 0.23 s for a 6,016-token cached prefix — which is why the 55k-prompt economics are survivable at all.
Both responses came back to curl as `HTTP 000` while the action had **landed**. Recorded as a runbook
(`docs/runbooks/verifier-model-server.md`) rather than prose in a pointer, because the next delegate will otherwise
spend a session rediscovering the endpoint set — two plausible-looking endpoints (`/api/v1/system`,
`/api/v1/loading`) do not exist on this build.

**And the process ruling, which is the larger one.** Today `complete_work` (`src/rig.mjs:931`) sets `done` in the
same commit as the author's own declaration, `evidence` is `Type.Optional`, and the same handler retires the item
worktree — so an item can be closed while its branch was never merged, which `docs/runbooks/land.md` records
happening twice (#3990, #4163). **ROADMAP 100** asked for the *measure* of that (branch tip not an ancestor of
`main` while the item reads `done`); the operator's ruling is the *gate*, registered as **253**: `done` requires a
cross-family verifier's re-runnable evidence **and** an artifact that is an ancestor of `main`, with the merge
mechanism staying `scripts/land.mjs`'s lock — because that runbook's own lesson is *when a mechanism replaces a
discipline, retire the discipline explicitly*. **217 lands first or 253 gets switched off**: a seat with no
spawnable shell cannot produce re-runnable evidence, and a gate that blocks everything is a gate that gets disabled.

**Also learned about instruments here, and it is worth a rule of its own:** eight of this instrument's findings were
findings **against itself** (`wc -l`, `md` matching before `mdx`, a backtick inside a URL, own-tree sizes scored hard, a
correction line, cross-citation families, fenced examples, and `--json` swallowing the next flag so `--top` became a
10,558-byte file literally named `--top` in the repo root). Every one is now a `--self-test` case. And a related
asymmetry: **`docs/ROADMAP.md` and `inputs/fetched/MANIFEST.md` have no executable reader** (re-confirmed: grepping
`demo/*.test.mjs` and `scripts/*.mjs` for them → nothing), so a duplicated item number or a malformed manifest row
leaves every test green — the cheap close is wiring `review-cite-check --gate` into the `check` rule (213's family).

## D164 — An instrument's **transport ceiling** masquerades as a model failure or a memory failure; measure both deadlines before believing any gate verdict — and the team restart is now conditioned on a **measured hygiene rehearsal** (2026-10-29, delegate measurement + one operator ruling)

**The ruling that matters most this session is the operator's, and it is a *condition*, not a date.** Asked whether the
team can start again — with the explicit hope of more throughput from more agents running at once — the operator
conditioned the restart on behaviour: seats must be hygienic about their **seat-personal workspace, git branches, git
worktrees, and regular merging of their branches back to `main` after a review**, and asked that this be *evaluated* at
the start of the next session. Registered as **ROADMAP 256**. What makes that a decision rather than a wish is that it
is answerable: the rig has instruments for the artifacts (`cli.mjs worktree audit` cross-references worktrees ↔ queue
items ↔ seat roots; the confine family; scratch-per-tree; `check`'s `shared-tree-on-main`, `stray-seat`,
`evidence-tree`; `land.md`/`merge.md`/`branch-cleanup.md`/`leaked-worktrees.md`; 100's ancestry measure and 253's
review-then-merge gate) and it has **no instrument that watches a seat do these things and counts violations**. That
gap is the row. And the reason the question cannot be answered from history is measurable: **20,340** `powershell` tool
calls, **0** `bash` calls, `spawn powershell ENOENT → 3` — on this host a seat has never run `git` or the demo suite, so
its hygiene is not good or bad, it is **unobserved** (217). Hence the ordering, which the next session should not
re-litigate: **217 (a seat must be able to run `git`) → 232 (the sweep that prunes the worktree ledger is the same code
family as the retire-on-`done` path 253 touches) → the hygiene audit → a 2-seat bounded rehearsal in the disposable
clone → an explicit operator threshold before scaling.** The payoff is priced in
`docs/reviews/wallclock-budget-2026-10-28.md`: resident-broker days waited **2.6–5.4 min** per claim and landed
**314–741 items/day** against **101.8–114.3 min** and 47–132/day for `run`-invoked days.

**The finding that overturns a previous session's diagnosis, recorded because the pointer asserted the wrong cause.**
Three model-probe runs "died partway with `REQUEST FAILED fetch failed` under memory pressure (swap 7/7 GB full)". The
cause is the **transport**: `tools/model-probes/gate.mjs:96` calls **non-streaming** `fetch`, llama-server sends the
response **headers** only when generation completes, and Node's global fetch default `headersTimeout` is **300 s**.
Matched pair, identical body, one variable (`.spike/gate/timeout-hypothesis.out`): global fetch → **300.8 s**,
`TypeError: fetch failed`, cause **`HeadersTimeoutError` [`UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT`]**; `node:http` with
`req.setTimeout(0)` → **HTTP 200 in 372.0 s**. `gate.mjs:426` prints only `e.message`, so the useful half of the error
never reached the operator or the pointer. Registered as **254**. The consequence is arithmetic, not mood: at the
measured **10.75 tok/s** the instrument's real output ceiling is **~3,200 tokens**, which is *below* what a reasoning
verifier needs — that, and not the box, is why 6 of 7 cells read `TRUNCATED-EMPTY` on 2026-10-28.

**The second deadline is the one that decides the verifier, and it is shorter than the first.** The provider path is
the `openai` SDK with a **600,000 ms** total request timeout plus 2 SDK retries (`src/config.mjs:222-262`, `:330-344`;
`DURIG_STREAM_TIMEOUT_MS` unset = platform default). `DURIG_VERIFIER_MAX_TOKENS: 8192` at 10.75 tok/s is a **762 s**
generation: **the rig declares an answer it cannot receive**, and `qa`'s p50 prompt (55,538 tok) at COLD prefill
(~212 tok/s) spends another **≈262 s** of the same window. Registered as **255**, in the same family as **208** (the
prompt side of the same arithmetic) — two sides of one measurement, not two rules that can disagree.

**And a capability fact about `recursivesi/flint` that no budget can work around.** LM Studio reports
`capabilities.reasoning: {allowed_options: ["on"], default: "on"}` — reasoning **cannot be turned off** — and two
route-arounds were **accepted and ignored**: at `max_tokens:1200` on a 20-line file with an explicit "answer in under
120 words" instruction, baseline / `chat_template_kwargs {thinking:false}` / top-level `thinking:false` all returned
`finish_reason=length` with **0 answer characters** (82.0 / 82.5 / 80.6 s), and at **4,000 tokens** the model spent
**17,554 characters on reasoning and emitted no answer**. So `TRUNCATED-EMPTY` is not a knob-tuning problem; on this
hardware the lever is **decode speed or model choice**. Q6_K's 32.72 GB cannot fit the 24 GB 3090 whole, which is *why*
decode is ~10 tok/s.

**What the operator granted, and the surface that does not exist.** The delegate was permitted to download flint
**`Q4_K_M`** (24,166,841,184 B; `POST /api/v1/models/download` requires a **HuggingFace URL**, not a model key — passing
`lmstudio-community/flint-GGUF` returns `Downloading community models as artifacts is not supported`). The file arrived
and registered as a third variant (`recursivesi/flint` variants: `@q6_k`, `@q8_0`, `@q4_k_m`), **but no documented
surface can activate a variant**: REST `load` rejects `variant`, `quantization` and `selected_variant`
(`Unrecognized key(s)`), `lms load` has no quantization flag and `lms load "recursivesi/flint@q4_k_m"` → `Model not
found`. Durable workarounds for the runbook: the bundled CLI only works at all with
`HOME=$HOME/.var/app/ai.lmstudio.lm-studio` (host-side it dies on `ENOENT …/lms-key-2`), and a second `unload` of an
already-gone instance returns **404** — an idempotency signal, not a failure. The rig was left **as found plus a
verified server**: Q6 reloaded at 65,536 and servable (`"READY"`, 32 completion tokens, 25.5 s — of which ~22 s was
cold-instance warm-up, itself a wall-clock fact worth pricing).

**Spool grant discharged; a new urgency found while landing the owed runbook.** The three intents
(`hygiene-rehearsal-20261029`, `verifier-merge-20261029`, `release-brief-20261028`) were spooled to **`pm`** via
`intent.mjs` with the broker down, so they queue and start nothing; decomposition stays `pm`'s. Landing the owed runbook
(`docs/runbooks/cross-clone-object-recovery.md`, + 2 rows in the runbook index — **Edit B discharged**) required
re-measuring the object store, which surfaced the urgent item: **452 unreachable commits** dated **2026-10-14 →
2026-10-21** (incl. `25008d8c` #1274, `5e00ee7e` #1558, `81005c62` #2111) sit in this checkout's store anchored by **no
ref**, past `gc.pruneExpire`'s default 2 weeks, while the clone that supplied them (`/mnt/d/Git/Durian-Pi`) is **not
mounted** — `git fsck --unreachable | grep -c '^unreachable commit'` = 452, `refs/rescued/*` = 32, `in-pack 22362`
across 2 packs. The minting grant (`refs/rescued/orphan-*`) is now time-critical rather than tidiness.

**A delegate-caused near-loss, logged because it is the same class as ROADMAP 233.** While appending this entry the
delegate used a whole-file write instead of an append and replaced **`docs/DECISIONS.md` (6,175 lines as it stood that day —
the file moves, so treat that as an incident-scale figure, not a current one) with 76**. It was recoverable in one command
**only because that file was committed**; the eight instruments lost in the 2026-10-28 incident were not committed and are
gone forever. Rule: a long append to a large committed file goes through an append, never a rewrite, and
`git status --short` + `wc -l` are read **after** the write verb, not before.

**Alternatives considered and rejected:** starting the channel now at 0 claimable rows (a started team idles or
improvises); treating "will they behave" as an operator judgement (the operator asked *when*, which is a dependency
question with measured costs); turning the verifier gate off to unblock 253 (**D137** — `check`'s green would be a lie);
and buying a bigger `max_tokens` for a model whose reasoning never ends. **Status:** the hygiene gate is **queued and
unevaluated** (256, next session's first item, spooled to `pm`); the verifier is **certified no more than before** and is
now additionally known to be **feasibility-bound by decode speed**; the pointer is corrected; no worktree or branch
changed (pre/post inventory diffed, `.spike` +1).

**D164 addendum, same session — the decode lever landed, and it moved the arithmetic without touching the capability
finding.** The operator granted the `Q4_K_M` download; the surface to *activate* it does not exist: REST `load`
rejects `variant`/`quantization`/`selected_variant` (`Unrecognized key(s)`; its body is `additionalProperties:false`),
`lms load` has no quantization flag, and `lms load "recursivesi/flint@q4_k_m"` → `Model not found`. **What works from
a shell:** unload by `instance_id`, **rename the other variants' `.gguf` files out of the scanned models tree** (same
filesystem ⇒ instant, reversible; nothing deleted — they sit at
`~/.var/app/ai.lmstudio.lm-studio/.lmstudio/set-aside-flint-q6-q8/`), then `load`; the catalog collapses to `@q4_k_m`
and the ordinary load body starts it. **Verified by the only surface that prints the truth** — `ps -eo args | grep
llama-server` → `--model …/flint-Q4_K_M.gguf` — because `GET /api/v1/models` reports the **same key** for every
variant. Result: **decode 10.75 → 42.21 tok/s** (1,500 tokens in 35.5 s), so the 300 s probe ceiling moves to ~12,600
output tokens, the rig's 600 s request deadline to ~25,200, and `DURIG_VERIFIER_MAX_TOKENS: 8192` from an impossible
**762 s** to a **194 s** generation; a k=1 gate run goes ~3 h → ~45 min. **This is why 255's defect is "a declared
budget with no measured speed behind it", not "762 s":** the number was a property of a *variant* the config never
named, and a claim about a model's speed is a claim about a quantization (acceptance **(5)** added to 255: name the
variant and the measured decode, or "we upgraded the verifier" is unfalsifiable). **What did not move:** the
unbounded-reasoning finding. On Q4 the model answers trivial prompts (`"Count from 1 to 900"` at 1,500 tokens → 1,715
answer chars; `"Reply with exactly: READY"` at 300 → `"READY"`, 89 reasoning chars) and still produces
**`answerChars=0`** on the four reasoning-lever arms at 1,200 tokens (3,491–4,236 reasoning chars), and the gate's
first cell — `H1-npm-invocation`, **defect** side — read **`TRUNCATED-EMPTY` at 6,000 tokens / 161.8 s** while **the
same file's clean control answered at 1,889 tokens / 42.6 s**. Read the asymmetry, not just the failure: this model
reasons hardest exactly where a verifier is being asked to find something, which is why a hello-world smoke test is
not evidence about the gate. Two facts about this box that earlier pointers did not state: **it has two GPUs** (16,376
MiB and 24,576 MiB), and **`unload` requires `instance_id`** when an instance is live (`{"model": …}` →
`missing_required_parameter`; the identical shape looked harmless earlier only because nothing was loaded and it
404'd). **Standing change to the rig, pending the operator's ratification:** the verifier is served from **Q4_K_M at
65,536**, with Q6_K/Q8_0 set aside — same model key, materially different model.

**D164 addendum 2 — the certification gate finished, and the defect it exposed was in the *instrument's* shape, not
only the model's (257).** For the first time a seeded-bug gate ran to completion on this box (24 prompts, Q4_K_M,
`CAL_MAX_TOKENS=6000`, fragment feeding, ~50 min, zero transport failures — which independently confirms 254's
fix-by-shim). The instrument printed **`defect items named: 1/1 scored (8 attempted)`** and, four lines away,
**`truncated (finish=length): 19 of 24 prompts`**. The line shaped like a score carries the flattering denominator,
and **253** would put that line in the path of `done`: a run in which 7 of 8 defect cells never reached an answer
would certify. Registered as **257** (scorability printed beside every rate; an INCONCLUSIVE floor — proposed ≥ ⅔ of
prompts per side reaching `finish=stop` — below which a gate consumer gets a non-zero exit rather than a percentage;
one predicate shared with 253 so the seat-facing verdict and the run record cannot disagree). Two findings that
changed my own reading and should change the next one: **every control that produced an answer produced a false
alarm** (leading 1/1, neutral 3/3) — so when the model finishes, it over-claims on clean code — **but two of those
alarms claimed missing imports on a fragment whose import block the window had cut off**, i.e. a correct inference
about the excerpt and a wrong claim about the file, a category `gate.mjs` already names (**195**) yet excused **0** of
because it excuses only turns making no code-level claim. So the honest verdict is not "flint is blind" (its one
scorable defect cell was `HIT+PHANTOM groups=3/3 need=2`, the first HIT this model recorded here) but **"it cannot
finish inside the budget, and what it finishes is miscalibrated"** — and the decisive next experiment is
**`--whole-module` over the fitting items and the three proof-backed mutants at ~10,000 output tokens (~30 min)**, not
another 6,000-token fragment run and not a purchase. **Rule extracted: before a control-side verdict counts against a
model, check whether the claim concerns material the run did not feed; and never accept a rate whose denominator is
smaller than the number of prompts attempted.**

## D165 — Six delegate asks become six operator grants: seat-root ruling A, a defined "queue drains", mint-before-`gc`, instrument hygiene, the verifier path (whole-module first, Q4_K_M ratified), and decomposition-not-seats with a stated scale threshold (2026-10-29, operator ruling; the delegate executes next session)

**The operator accepted all six recommendations and directed that they be executed in the next session**, which converts
six open asks into grants with owners and costs. Recorded here because the *why* is what the next session cannot re-derive.

**(1) ROADMAP 221 — ruling A is the ruling:** the persisted per-seat root becomes the workspace-root-relative name, `up --root`
once per seat, **no migration code**. Chosen over a migration because the value is only wrong for future seats on this host and
a migration would rewrite history-bearing config for no benefit; and it is not a cosmetic ruling — `classifyGitRoot("D:\Git\Durian-Pi-worktrees\engineer")`
prints **`main-worktree`** on Linux, and **256**'s hygiene audit cannot score a seat's workspace discipline while the seat root
is an unreadable cross-machine path. Implementation is the team's (failing-first demo in `src/`), not the delegate's.
**(2) "The queue drains" gets a two-clause predicate, not a count:** *every released row reaches a terminal state within one
resident-broker day* (the 314–741 items/day regime from `docs/reviews/wallclock-budget-2026-10-28.md`) **and** *no `held` row
older than **7 days** survives a `pm` pass without being released or explicitly cancelled*. A bare "claimable == 0" definition
was rejected on measurement: the queue is **4,821 rows / 0 claimable**, so such a definition would declare the queue
permanently non-draining and make the clause an unpassable gate on #725/#726/#727 (already `held` 12 days). The product half
is **231**; releases stay `pm`'s verb, so those three rows remain `held` until the predicate exists and `pm` releases them.
**(3) Minting `refs/rescued/orphan-*` is granted, and the grant is deliberately split from 232.** Minting is reversible,
cheap (one `git update-ref` each) and closes a real decay window — **452 unreachable commits dated 2026-10-14→10-21**
(`25008d8c` #1274, `5e00ee7e` #1558, `81005c62` #2111) sit anchored by no ref past `gc.pruneExpire`, with the supplying clone
unmounted; deletion stays a separate decision. Reassuringly-measured: this store has **267 loose objects** against
`gc.auto`'s 6,700 threshold, so an auto-gc will not fire on its own — the exposure is a human or seat running `git gc`, which
is exactly what the next session's first command closes. **232 remains gated** on the 241 design note: nobody touches
`src/worktree.mjs:649` / `src/broker.mjs:1167`, and no suite runs from this checkout while it is open.
**(4) Instrument hygiene (233) is scoped, not deferred:** land the one shim that earned it (`.spike/gate/no-headers-timeout.mjs`
→ `tools/model-probes/`, labelled as such until **254** replaces it properly), label the other two
`instrument-provenance` lists under **UNTRACKED BUT CITED** as **re-created** or amend the rows that cite them, then gitignore
`.scratch/` (**38 files**). The rationale is this session's own evidence twice over: the 2026-10-28 instruments that were
never committed are gone forever, while today's destroyed-then-restored `docs/DECISIONS.md` (6,175 lines → 76 → 6,175 by one
`git checkout --`) survived **only because it was committed**. Untracked work is work that can vanish; committed work cannot.
**(5) The verifier path is (a) then (c), and the Q4_K_M serving change is ratified.** First the **`--whole-module` mutant run**
(~30 min, removes the excerpt confound, targets the three proof-backed mutants); only if that still false-alarms on controls
does the rig pay for a **remote cross-family verifier**, which is the only option satisfying **253** today. Bigger budgets
(k=3 at ~10,000 tokens, ~2.5 h) are explicitly **not** funded before (a) resolves the confound, and starting uncertified is
ruled out on **D137** grounds. The Q4_K_M switch (Q6/Q8 set aside by rename, restorable with one `mv`) is kept because 3.9×
decode is what makes any local verifier discussable — with the standing caveat that **the model key did not change while the
model did**, which is why 255 acceptance (5) now demands variant + measured decode in every run record.
**(6) Decomposition starts, seats do not; the scale threshold is accepted as proposed.** The channel stays down because the
queue has **0 claimable** rows — a started team would idle or improvise (and at 5 seats the broker already spent **48.5 %** of a
window in `askSeat` with **42.9 %** of dispatches `no_healthy_seat`, so "more seats" is not "more throughput" by construction).
Scale gate: **zero violations of the hard dimensions** (no leaked worktree, no stray seat, no branch unmerged while its item
reads `done`) over the bounded 2-seat rehearsal, **≤2 soft violations per seat-run**, then 5 seats with the audit re-run, then
12. The numbers come from the operator's own restart condition, made measurable by **256**.

**Consequence the operator should see plainly: the RTX 3090 was never the verifier's constraint.** The seats live on the other
card (`strata-host`, `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S`, 14.6 GB on the A4000), so the 3090 is effectively a dedicated verifier box.
The binding constraints are (i) flint's non-terminating reasoning under an output budget, and (ii) **D137's cross-family rule**,
which disqualifies the fastest single-card models — the Qwen3 MoE family — precisely because the seats are Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.
That is why **258** is registered (answer-first contracts, forced-choice scoring, structured output, `llama-server`-direct flags,
and a context/`parallel` reconfiguration that returns KV bytes to weights) and why the candidate list in
`docs/runbooks/verifier-model-server.md` names `gpt-oss-20b`, `mistral-small-3.x-24b` and `gemma-3-27b` rather than the
bigger Qwen quants. Relaxing D137 to admit a same-family verifier remains the operator's ruling to make, and this entry records
the cost of making it: a verifier that shares a family shares its blind spots. **Status:** grants recorded, pointer re-cut to
§OPERATOR GRANTS (the superseded §OPERATOR OWES is archived verbatim); nothing executed yet; nothing pushed.

## D166 — Both local verifier candidates are now measured and rejected; the "flint thinks too much" story was substantially a *host instruction* and an *excerpt artifact*; and the 452 orphan commits are anchored (2026-10-29, operator's model swap + delegate measurement)

**What the operator changed and what I corrected.** The operator unloaded flint and loaded
`mistralai/ministral-3-14b-reasoning` **Q6_K**, then asked that things be configured correctly. They were not:
`durig.config.json` pointed at `recursivesi/flint` — an **unloaded** model, so any verifier request would have made LM Studio
re-offload a 24 GiB model onto a card already at 23.0/24.5 GiB — and it declared `DURIG_VERIFIER_CONTEXT 65536` against an
instance launched `--ctx-size 8192 --parallel 4`, with `DURIG_VERIFIER_MAX_TOKENS 8192`, i.e. a request that cannot be
satisfied (prompt + 8,192 output > 8,192 total). Now: model `mistralai/ministral-3-14b-reasoning`, context `8192`,
max tokens `3000`. Registered as **259**, with a fixture for the impossible pair, because nothing in `check` catches it.

**(1) The unbounded-thinking instruction is the host's, not the model's.** LM Studio's generated chat template sets a *default
system message when the request carries none*: *"First draft your thinking process (inner monologue) until you arrive at a
response… Be as casual and as long as you want…"*. Matched pair on ministral Q6_K, `temperature 0`: no system message →
400/400 tokens, `finish=length`, `content=0ch`; with a bounding system message → **1.9 s, `finish=stop`, 62 tokens, correct
verdict, `reasoning=0ch`**; raising that arm's budget to 1,200 changed nothing. Four request-level reasoning toggles were
ignored. **Why it matters:** for days the budget was the thing being adjusted, and for requests without a system message the
budget was never the variable — the instruction was. Every durig-initiated completion must carry a system message.
**(2) `flint`'s "4/4 false alarms on clean controls" was mostly our instrument, and I withdraw it.** Three of four alarms were
true statements about the excerpt my window showed — `existsSync`/`join`/`readFileSync` are imported at
`src/worktree.mjs:11,13`; `isWindows` is declared at `src/job-object.mjs:30`; `clockin.mjs:27-29` imports all five the model
named — and `corpus.mjs:250` already warned that windowing manufactures exactly these. The runner excuses an artifact turn only
when it makes *no* code-level claim, so truth about my scaffolding scored as a judgement failure. The fourth cell's actual
verdict was *"No — there's no defect…"* and was still counted an alarm for volunteering a wrong aside. Corrected restatement:
flint's clean side has **≤1 genuine judgement failure**, its one scorable defect cell was a **HIT with the correct mechanism**,
and its real failure is **non-termination**.
**(3) Non-termination is a runaway loop, so a larger budget is the wrong lever.** Answered cells: 787–5,275 tokens, mean 4-gram
repetition **0.13**, `dupLines=0/31`. Truncated cells: all stopped at exactly the ceiling, mean repetition **0.27**, with the
same hypothesis repeated **34×**, **314** duplicate sentences, `dupLines=168/402` — and mid-reasoning passages arguing about
irrelevant JavaScript syntax. The rig detects this class for seats (`src/degeneration.mjs`) and not for the model under probe.
**(4) Ministral is operationally excellent and judgmentally unfit: measured and rejected.** 24/24 cells answered, 137–464
tokens, 4.5–15.7 s, **31.6 tok/s**, zero truncations — but **0/16 clean controls**: it committed `VERDICT: DEFECT` for every
control, and reversing the contract's option order did not change that (0/8 in the control arm). Its mechanisms are invented
(`process.kill(pid,0)` supposedly fails for kernel threads/zombies; `toISOString()` supposedly emits non-UTC when the clock is
unsynced — it cannot). Mechanism credit **HIT 2/8**. So the answer-first contract is **not** a free improvement: on a
defect-prior model it converts vague hedging into a decisively wrong verdict 16/16 times, which is worse for routing than the
hedging it replaced. Acceptance now gated on a clean-control calibration check (**258** follow-up).
**Consequence the operator should weigh:** the two candidates fail in opposite directions — flint answers 5/24 but was the
better-calibrated of the two, ministral answers 24/24 and is wrong every time on clean input. **Neither satisfies 253 today**,
so the only option satisfying it now is a **remote cross-family verifier**; the cheap remaining local lever is a flint re-run
under corrected conditions (bounded system message in the gate's own `SYSTEM` constant, which has never been varied;
declaration-header or whole-module feeding — whole modules in this corpus are 1,686–22,014 est. tokens, so `--whole-module`
needs ctx ≥ 24k at `--parallel 1`; my earlier "58,380 est. tokens for H4" was a misread of the pair-accounting **chars**
column). Do **not** route ministral: `check` would then clear on a string comparison while verification got worse, which is the
exact failure D137 was written to prevent.
**Accountability, recorded because it constrains future probe work.** My arms helped OOM-kill the **seats'** server (`strata`).
Swap was already 8/8 GiB used; I ran repeated arms against a 65,536-context flint Q4 instance with `strata-host` resident on the
other card, plus `buildCorpus()` (a parse-check subprocess per candidate window) alongside, and I did not re-measure headroom
between arms. Discipline now in the runbook: pre-flight print of available RAM / swap / per-GPU MiB with a named floor, one arm
at a time, never a corpus build concurrent with a generation arm, one large-context engine resident.
**Executed from the grants.** **GRANT 3 is done and verified**: `refs/rescued/orphan-<sha>` minted for all **452** unreachable
commits; `refs/rescued` 32 → **484**; `git fsck --unreachable | grep -c '^unreachable commit'` → **0**; sample resolutions
`orphan-0030993f5abe` ("merge: land devtools-item-4436 onto main"), `orphan-0102f3c23b1c` ("seatguard: refuse silent write
corruption (#673)"). Reversible by `update-ref -d`; nothing was deleted, and **232 stays gated**. GRANT 5 partially executed:
ministral measured, so the "which verifier" question is now evidence-shaped rather than speculative.

**D167 (2026-10-29). Memory safety is an instrument, not a rule of thumb; and the OS message blaming "the background service run-p2756020-i2781901.scope" is read as containment, not as an incident.**
*What was decided and what shipped:* `tools/model-probes/probe-preflight.mjs` (MemAvailable, swap %, per-GPU free MiB, every resident model server's RSS **and its shmem**, its served `--ctx-size`/`--parallel`/`--resident-experts`, and the rig's declared verifier ctx vs max-tokens; exits 1 under the floor) and `tools/model-probes/capped-run.mjs` (starts the arm in its own systemd scope and prints the scope's peak and whether the cap fired) — registered as **260**; and **261** for the dead-pointer gap: `cli.mjs check` and `single-model-rig` both passed while all five verifier seats in `rig.selfdev.json` pointed at `verifier/recursivesi/flint` and the only loaded instance was `Ministral-3-14B-Reasoning-2512-Q6_K.gguf`. `demo/local-model-pointer.test.mjs` is the guard that fails, so it is now named in the verifier runbook as a post-swap gate.
*Why an instrument and not prose:* the kernel executed the **seats' server** for a sin a probe committed — `esbuild invoked oom-killer`, then `Out of memory: Killed process 2289527 (strata-host) total-vm:132182136kB, anon-rss:53969596kB, oom_score_adj:200` — because the OOM killer scores by size, and this box's largest process is a model server by an order of magnitude. Prose thresholds ("be careful with RAM") had already failed: my own arms were running when it died.
*Why those numbers:* no existing surface printed the footprint that matters. The IQ3_S pack is **52 GB + 27 GB** of GGUF; `strata-host` held **50.3 GiB RSS of which 40.7 GiB was `Pss_Shmem`**, while only **12.6 GiB** of it sat on GPU0. GPU1 was **94 %** full. Swap is **zram only, 8 GiB, ~78 % consumed** — so the ceiling we hit is swap, not RAM, and a verifier that "needs only 8 GiB" is not free.
*Why `MemorySwapMax=0` is the default:* measured, because the naive cap is a placebo. With `MemoryMax=300M MemorySwapMax=1G` a 600 MiB page-touched job **survived** — `MemoryMax` caps RAM only and the extra allowance is the box's scarce swap. With `MemorySwapMax=0` the same job printed *"the CAP fired — the arm was killed inside its own scope"* and afterwards `strata-host` was still resident at 52,739,964 kB and `llama-server` at 3,926,924 kB. Second measured trap: `Buffer.alloc` is zero-filled lazily, so allocating without touching pages never trips a cap (400 × 1 MiB passed a 300 MB cap) — a guard tested that way is a placebo, so the proof must use `b.fill(1)`.
*Why the operator-facing reading matters:* the desktop notification the operator received named `run-p2756020-i2781901.scope`, which was **my** capped test arm, journal-confirmed at `200M memory peak` with `Failed with result 'oom-kill'`, while both servers kept running (RSS 52,712,604 → 52,602,224 kB, unchanged instance uptime). A `run-<digits>.scope` kill **is the guard working**; an `app-…appimage@…service` or a `strata`/`llama-server` kill is the incident. Telling the operator "the kernel killed something" without that distinction manufactures panic and hides the result.
*Also recorded, because it cost time and will recur:* an edit to `docs/ROADMAP.md` reported `Successfully replaced 1 block(s)` and **never wrote** (mtime still at the previous commit) — so every write is now verified with `grep -c` + `stat` + `git status`; and a `cat > … <<'EOF'` whose body contained an example ending in a bare `EOF` **terminated its own heredoc** and executed the rest of the document as shell. Both are now `docs/runbooks/delegate-doc-hygiene.md`, indexed in the runbook README.
*Blind spots:* cgroup2 delegation is confirmed for systemd-managed units, **not** for the systemd user instance's own children (`user.slice` has an empty `cgroup.procs` on this kernel — a reporting quirk, so read the unit's journal line for its peak); and a `--vram-reserve-mib`/`--max-context` change to the **seat** server trades seat output quality for headroom, which is the operator's call, not a delegate's.
*Do not:* raise a seat server's context to accommodate the verifier — they contend for the same host RAM and the same box; and do not call a probe "contained" because it finished.
