**D171 (2026-10-30). An operator ruling a guard cannot express is not a ruling — instrument the exception, do not bypass the guard; and the closed loop D169 named is open, at a measured price.**

**What the operator decided.** Asked for one bounded, coordinator-scoped `pm` wake (OWES 1), the operator answered **"yes"**
at 2026-10-30T04:2xZ. This is the first operator grant in this rig's history that a preflight then refused to execute.

**1. The finding is about the instrument, not the loop.** `node tools/broker-serve.mjs --start --yes-pm-wakes
--max-duration 600` printed **`START REFUSED: seat-shell-availability`**. `--yes-pm-wakes` acknowledges the *spool*
(D147 §1) and `--allow-dirty` acknowledges the *tree*; **`seat-shell-availability` had no ack flag at all**, so the start was
refused *no matter what the operator decided*. A preflight exists to make an operator-owned hazard visible before a write;
a hazard the operator has ruled on and the tool still cannot record turns the preflight into a veto it does not own. That is
the second face of D169's loop: the loop was not only "no row exists", it was **"the ruling has no representation."**

**2. The exception is measured, never asserted.** `--ack-coordinator-wake` does not waive the block. For every seat in the
predicted first-pass wake set it asks the product's own `toolRemovalsFor` (`src/seattools.mjs:249`, `COORDINATOR_REMOVALS`)
whether that seat keeps the shell tool. A seat that loses its shell also loses `read`/`write`/`edit`/`prepare_workspace`, so
for exactly those seats the absent shell guards an act that runs no command and lands no artifact. Applied to the live rig
file (Linux, `label-withheld-per-D205`, node v24.22.1): **`pm` and `lead` are coordinators** (`keepsShell=false`); **the other ten
keep the shell** — so the downgrade is neither vacuous nor general, and it requires `--max-duration`. Measured behaviour:
without the ack `--dry-run` exits **1**; with it, the finding becomes a NOTE; `--start` with the ack and no `--max-duration`
exits **2**; and after the spool emptied of intents the ack **correctly declined** (an empty wake set is absence of evidence,
not evidence nobody shell-needing wakes).
*Why not just run `cli.mjs serve` directly:* that skips every other check in the preflight and leaves no record. The pointer's
own line — "name the exception, do not bypass the guard" — was followed by **giving the exception a name**.

**3. Two wake semantics I had to learn out loud, and they are the cheap part of future sessions.** (a) **Delivered ≠ woken**:
`INTENT delivered=6 dead=0 dup=0` and every pass still logged `SKIP pm reason=pending conv=3` — the **per-seat suppression**
variant (runbook `broker-down-or-stalled.md` case (b), one-seat variant), discriminated by fresh `heartbeatAt` + frozen
`lastPassAt` + no `genlock` + GPU0 at 0 %. Remedy: **stop → `resume` (broker STOPPED) → restart**; `resume` found **9** and
withdrew them. (b) **`resume` cancels in-flight generations.** Six of the withdrawn submissions were `pm`'s remaining
queued generations, which is why turn one produced 26 rows (**#4820–#4845**) on the memory/LINUX-track numbering and **zero**
of the portability class. Completing the granted act needed a second coordinator turn via
`cli.mjs send pm --body-file … --request-id …` (settled `done`). **`send` prints a DEPRECATION warning: it opens a full
writing harness = a second owner.** It was admissible only because no broker was running; the sanctioned path stays
`intent.mjs` + a startable broker. **Do not reach for `send` while a broker drives.**

**4. What the wake bought, measured by instruments rather than by my narration.** Queue rows **4,821 → 4,861**;
**CLAIMABLE 0 → 16**; `tools/roadmap-queue-coverage.mjs` items ≥200 named by a row **1 → 15**, no-row **67 → 53**.
`pm` minted ONE seam: **263 #4847 → 217 #4849 → 264 #4851 → 221 #4852 + 265 #4854 → 266 #4853 → 267 #4855 → 256 #4857**, with
**232 #4850** gated on the 241 note (**#4846**, which it minted as an artifact because the note had no row to hang a gate on),
**233 #4848**, thin ranges **#4859–#4861**, and **#4858** (`lead`) registering the missing **landing plan**. It **revised
#4840/#4842 in place** ("folded into 263/221 and 217/264 — hold on claim") instead of forking a second seam, and registered
**#4856** when `hold_work` refused a row it had created while `release_work` succeeded as sender — one-way authority. It also
**reversed its own earlier `#3350` release** rather than release into an unworkable class. That is the discipline this rig
exists to produce, and it happened under a 600-second window.

**5. The price, and it goes on the record as a soft violation, not a clean run.** Inside that window, three repo-root
directories named for another OS's absolute path appeared — **`C:`**, **`C:\Users\Alex\dsh-Projects\pi-opendurig`**, and
**`…\item-4789`** — holding `.durig/queue-{all,security,scribe,impl}.md`: harness per-seat views written into the foreign
persisted cwds (221 made visible). Proven by **name diff** (`.spike/pre-wake-root.txt`, 67 entries → exactly 3 new, zero
tracked changes, zero losses), preserved by **moving** to `.spike/evidence-phantom-roots-20261029/` (6 files). **They are
invisible to `git status`, because `.gitignore:12` is `.durig/`, which matches at any depth** — so a clean `git status` is
NOT evidence a seat wrote nowhere, and the filesystem scan (`phantom-seat-root-path`) is the only surface that sees this
class. This is the same shape the 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-28 incidents recorded. **Measured distinction that decides the
exception:** `pm`'s turn wrote **none** of them; only **file-capable** seats produce them — the coordinator exception holding
in the wild, not just in the predicate.

**6. The standing conclusion, and it is uncomfortable.** Opening the channel **worked** and the team **did** decompose. But
the result of decomposition is **16 `queued` rows on a host where no registered shell exists and all 12 seat roots are
foreign** — so `--ack-coordinator-wake` now refuses any further wake by design, and the honest reading is: **a claimable row
is not a runnable row.** The rig's bottleneck moved from "nothing is tracked" to "the work is tracked and this machine cannot
execute it." 217 and 221 are therefore not hygiene items any more; they are the gate on whether this box can run its own
team at all, and #4858 (the release order) is the next real decision.

**Falsifiable next session.** `ls -A | grep -E '^[A-Za-z]:|\\|dsh-Projects'` must print **nothing**; if it prints anything,
a seat woke and 221 fired again — name-diff against `.spike/pre-wake-root.txt` before touching it.
`tools/roadmap-queue-coverage.mjs` must not regress below **15 named / 53 no-row**. If a delegate runs
`--start --yes-pm-wakes` and reports "the operator granted it", they did not read this decision: **`--yes-pm-wakes` does not
acknowledge `seat-shell-availability`.** If anyone calls this session's run "green", they did not count the phantom dirs.

**D172 (2026-10-30). The seat-root half of the portability class is closed by an OPERATING act, not by code: the operator grants an isolated Linux worktree of `main` as this rig's seat root, `DURIG_SEAT_ROOT` + bulk `up --refresh` applies it, and the rig's own portability instrument drops 15 findings to 2 — with two named costs (five stale-model resets, and one shared root for twelve seats) that ROADMAP 221 removes and no delegate may treat as settled.**

**1. What was decided, and why this shape.** Last session's standing conclusion (D171 §6) was that a claimable row is not a runnable row on this box. The class that makes it runnable — 263's resolver, 217's shell, 221's per-seat root, 266's keep-guard — cannot be worked by seats that have no root and no shell. The operator ruled the deadlock is broken on **this** host, in an **isolated worktree of `main`**, not on the Windows box where the tools are native. That choice matters: the alternative (work it where the shell works) leaves the Linux checkout permanently delegate-only, and the operator rejected that.

**2. The mechanism, measured, because the docs disagree about it.** `docs/DECISIONS.md:6314` grants an `up --root` flag that **does not exist**. The working mechanism is the environment chain at `cli.mjs:679` (`seatCwd = seat.cwd ?? spec.cwd ?? CFG.DURIG_SEAT_ROOT`, written only when defined): with `DURIG_SEAT_ROOT` exported, `up rig.selfdev.json --refresh` previews and writes `cwd` for **12/12** seats; without it, it writes **nothing** about cwd (12 seats report `{}` or a model change only). So `--refresh` alone repairs nothing about the root — the export is load-bearing, and `--dry-run` with the export is the step that names the whole repair before it lands.

**3. The verifier of the repair is the instrument, not `ps`.** `node tools/rig-portability-audit.mjs` went **15 findings → 2** on the same tree, and **the 232 `seat-root-unmatchable` finding cleared as a side effect**: with the stored roots pointing at a *registered* worktree, the keep-guard's exact normalized-string equality matches again, so `keepReason: "seat-root"` is reachable on this host for the first time since the machine move. The two survivors are both ROADMAP 217. `--self-test` exit 0 throughout. The safety evidence is the name-diff (worktrees + branches + `.spike`): **4 added lines, zero deletions**, live tree clean, store backed up to `.spike/repoint-20261030/`.

**4. Two costs the grant accepted, stated so nobody re-trades them blind.** (a) `--refresh` is all-twelve and applies the rig file's models: the STORE carried `local/iq3_s` for `qa, qa2, advocate, auditor, designer` while `rig.selfdev.json` names `verifier/ministral-3-14b-reasoning`, so the re-point cost **five conversation resets** (`resetEntryId` 275003/275005/275007/275009/275011). A store/rig model divergence is invisible to every read surface except `up --dry-run`. (b) **Twelve seats now share one root.** That is the F21 hazard in a repair costume, accepted only because the alternative is no root at all, mitigated only by per-item `prepare_workspace` trees and by this being an isolated tree rather than the live checkout. **221's per-seat root is the fix, and this decision is a stopgap on top of it, not a substitute for it.**

**5. The bottleneck moved again, and it is now exactly one item.** With the roots repaired, 217 is the only thing this rig's own instrument complains about — and 217 is what makes every other row unverifiable by its author (22 `spawn … ENOENT` shell results, newest entry #274427). That is an argument for lead to rule 217's release order explicitly, which is what #4858 asks.

**6. The instrument that records the operator's ruling is INERT for the product's own intents, measured.** `tools/broker-serve.mjs:322` computes the ack's wake set as `pending.filter((p) => p.to !== "?" && p.op === "?")` — it counts only spool files with **no `op` field**. The product's own producer (`intent.mjs`) writes `{"op":"message", …}`, and the broker itself defaults a missing op to `"message"` (`src/broker.mjs:421`). So real message intents are invisible, the computed wake set is empty, and `--ack-coordinator-wake` can never be measured admissible: a `--start --yes-pm-wakes --ack-coordinator-wake --max-duration 600` against a spool holding exactly two coordinator messages is **REFUSED** on `seat-shell-availability` with no admissibility suffix at all. D169's remedy is therefore unexecuted in practice, and the fix is one seam (ask the broker's own `intentOp()` what the op is), failing-first, not a fourth hand-rolled filter.

**7. And a second, independent reason the same start must refuse even once the filter is fixed:** with 16 claimable rows addressed across 10 seats, the first-pass wake set is **not** coordinator-only — the product's own `toolRemovalsFor` says `pm` and `lead` are the only seats with the shell removed (`architect` keeps it: capability `review`; so `review` is a WORKING_CAPABILITY and "coordinator" is not a name for `architect`/`designer`/`advocate`/`auditor`/`security`). A broker start therefore cannot be made coordinator-scoped while the claimable head stands; the only bootstrap that wakes exactly the coordinators is `cli.mjs send` with **no broker running**, which is deprecated as a second harness owner and admissible only for that reason.

**Falsifiable next session.** `node tools/rig-portability-audit.mjs` must report **2 findings, both 217** — if it reports 12 `seat-root-unresolvable`, the store's roots went foreign again (name the tree, do not trust `ps`, which prints no cwd). `git worktree list --porcelain` must show **2** registered worktrees. `ls -A | grep -E '^[A-Za-z]:|\\|dsh-Projects'` must print nothing. If anyone starts the broker with `--ack-coordinator-wake` and reports it worked, ask them to show the admissibility suffix — a bare `--start` past a BLOCK is not the grant.

## D173 — 217 closes by ONE REGISTRY that separates "can START" from "is PREFERRED" (2026-10-30; authored by seat `impl`, verified by the delegate; **NOT landed on `main`**)

**The why.** 217 did not fail because the rig picked the wrong shell. It failed because **two surfaces each kept their own private answer to "what is a shell"**: `src/seattools.mjs` registered exactly one hardcoded tool
(`createPowerShellTool()`), while `src/seatguard.mjs` kept its own literal set of shell-tool NAMES for the one decision it cares about — which tool calls carry a command string worth inspecting. On the Windows host the two copies
happened to agree, so the duplication was invisible; the move to Linux broke them **in the same direction, twice**: the registered tool's programs (`pwsh`, then `powershell`) do not exist here, so every seat shell call was a spawn
ENOENT (22 such results in the store, newest entry #274427, and `tools/channel-preflight.mjs` §7 printing "NO SHELL CAN START HERE"), while `bash`, which *does* exist, was unreachable because nothing registered it — yet the guard
already whitelisted the name `bash`. **The guard was inspecting a tool that was not a tool.** So the fix is not "add bash": it is one registry, read by both surfaces, keeping two questions apart — `canStart(host)` (is the program
launchable here; a PATH SCAN, never a spawn, because the module is imported by the CLI, the broker, the seat harness and `tools/rig-portability-audit.mjs`, and the selection runs at module load) versus `preferredOn(host)` (which shell
this host gets when more than one can start). The 217 failure was a *preference* that was correct for Windows, applied where the program could not *start*.

**What was deliberately NOT folded in, and why.** lead's rejected edge (#4864 item 3): a host-OS or per-seat-shell field is **store schema** (the D24 / #3506 family, the axis #3456 wants explicit) and it changes what 263/264 read. So
the schema half is its own row, **#4879** (architect). impl held that boundary and said so. The measured cost of the split is visible in the gate: `tools/rig-portability-audit.mjs` went **2 findings → 1**, and the survivor is
`seat-host-unaware` — i.e. **217 is genuinely half-closed**, and the instrument proves it rather than the prose claiming it.

**Evidence (delegate-run, Linux host `label-withheld-per-D205`, 2026-10-30T07:0xZ, in `/home/chexxor/Git/durian-dev/seatroot`):** `seatTools.shell.name` resolves to **`bash`**; the audit run from that tree against the real store prints **1
finding** (`seat-host-unaware`) and **`seat-shell-availability` is gone**, while the same command from the live checkout still prints 2 — because `main` does not have the change, and *that difference is the measurement*. GREEN:
`demo/seattools.test.mjs`, `demo/seatguard.test.mjs`, `demo/ctxline.test.mjs` exit 0. **RED verified, not assumed:** the delegate reverted `src/seattools.mjs` + `src/seatguard.mjs` to HEAD and moved `src/shellregistry.mjs` aside —
`demo/seatguard.test.mjs` then fails on a **substantive assertion** ("the degraded-cwd shell refusal NAMES the verb it refused and the shell registered on this host"), while `demo/seattools.test.mjs` fails **only by a missing import**.
Whether an import-failure RED counts as failing-first is an OPEN question the delegate refused to settle alone, and the verifier briefed to judge it could not be woken (below). All five files were restored **byte-identically**
(`sha256sum -c`: OK).

**Full-suite attribution (238 demos × 2 trees).** `main` fails 4 (`broker-stop-audit`, `deepinfra-catalog`, `dry-run`, `init`); the seat root fails 3 (`clockin-digest`, `deepinfra-catalog`, `local-model-pointer`). The divergent pairs are
tree-shaped, not change-shaped: `local-model-pointer` asserts a *configured* `local` provider, and the seat root has **no `./durig.config.json`** at all (the audit's own note: "a moved workspace has no host config at all");
`clockin-digest` runs `git rev-list --count main..(no branch)`, which cannot resolve on a **detached** worktree. Re-running both against the real store still fails, confirming host-config rather than store. **No regression is
attributable to the change.** The durable lesson: when you isolate a seat root you must also give it the host layer, or the suite starts measuring the tree instead of the code.

**The verifier leg is blocked at the host, and that is now load-bearing rather than theoretical.** `qa` could not be woken at all: two sends (a ~7k-char brief and a 1.1k-char brief) both returned `settledReason: model_error` with no
reply, and the mechanism is measured — a direct request to the served model is refused with `exceed_context_size_error: request (9129 tokens) exceeds the available context size (8192 tokens), try increasing it`. The verifier slot on
this box is **n_ctx 8192**, so a real verifier conversation cannot fit; `compact qa` also fails (`no compaction entry was written for seat qa`) because compaction needs the same window. This upgrades ROADMAP **208** from a design
concern to a **hard failure of the ratified loop** (impl authors → delegate runs the oracle → qa reviews): the first two legs worked, the third cannot. Raising the served context is a **host-side** change on a GPU already at

**And the approved root decays once per coordinator completion.** `complete_work` re-points a seat's PERSISTED cwd to `process.cwd()` of whichever process served the wake (`src/rig.mjs:1047-1051`; the product already calls that cwd

## D174 — the verifier leg was killed by a ROLE SEQUENCE plus migration residue, not by its context window; raising the window was necessary and is not sufficient (delegate, 2026-10-30, Linux)

**What the previous record claimed, and why it had to be re-opened.** D173 recorded the dead verifier leg as `n_ctx 8192`: both `send qa`
attempts returned `model_error` with no reply, and a direct request to the served model was refused with `exceed_context_size_error:
request (9129 tokens) exceeds the available context size (8192 tokens)`. That measurement was real. The *attribution* was wrong, and
re-testing it in one command falsifies it: the seat request the harness sends the verifier is refused **before** the window is ever
reached, in ~30 ms with zero tokens generated, by the chat template — `Engine protocol predict request returned 500 … Jinja Exception:
After the optional system message, conversation roles must alternate user and assistant roles except for tool calls and results.` The
check is LM Studio's own: lines 43-52 of the template it generated for this model
(`.lmstudio/.internal/temp/lmstudio-chat-template-*/chat-template.jinja`, preceded by the comment `Checks for alternating user/assistant messages.`).

**The shape that triggers it, pinned at its minimum.** After a clean `cli.mjs reset qa` **with no handoff**, the outgoing conversation is
three messages — `system, user, user` — and that alone is enough: the `reset <seat> <handoff>` handoff is a **user** turn and `send` appends
another. So the product writes consecutive user roles in its normal operation, and a strict-template model refuses them outright.

**Why the rig tolerated this until now.** The residue predates the provider move. Counting `pi.user` / `pi.assistant` entries per seat
(`cli.mjs log <seat> --limit 400`): qa 184 user turns / 193 errored assistant turns / **1** assistant turn carrying any text; qa2 189/189/1;
auditor 158/159/**0**; pm 140; lead 181; impl 157. 180 of qa's errors read `402: {"message":"You need positive balance to do inference` —
this rig's verifier used to be a **paid cloud provider**, those turns never got answers, and the store came over in the Windows→Linux move
while the answers did not. The local provider (Strata `iq3_s`, declared window 200,000) accepts consecutive user turns, which is why the
local seats look healthy and only the verifier cannot wake at all. Read this as migration residue meeting a strict template, i.e. a member
of the same portability class as 217/221/263/265 — not as a model-capacity problem.

**What was changed on the host, by the operator's explicit instruction to use LM Studio's own API.** `lms unload` then
`lms load mistralai/ministral-3-14b-reasoning -c 16384 --parallel 1 --gpu max` (the CLI shipped in LM Studio's own package, reached with
`HOME` pointed at the flatpak's `.lmstudio`; the app's REST surface on `:1234` exposes only `GET /api/v0/models` on this build — `POST`,
`PATCH`, `PUT`, `DELETE` on that route all answer `Unexpected endpoint or method`). Before: `--ctx-size 8192 --parallel 4`; after: `--ctx-size 16384 --parallel 1`,
confirmed three ways — `/api/v0/models` reports `loaded_context_length: 16384`, the new `llama-server` cmdline reads `--ctx-size 16384 --parallel 1`,
and the identical 9,627-token probe that returned **HTTP 400** now returns **HTTP 200** with a completion. The rig's `DURIG_VERIFIER_CONTEXT`
was corrected from `8192` to `16384` in the gitignored host config so the declared window stops lying. GPU arithmetic, computed from the
model file's own metadata (`.spike/gguf-arch.mjs`, 40 layers × 8 KV heads × (128+128) × 2 B at `--cache-type-k/v f16` = **160 KiB/token**):
8192×4 = 5.00 GiB of KV, 16384×1 = 2.50 GiB — the raise *shrinks* the pool. Measured footprint on GPU0 went 12,648 → 13,914 MiB.
LM Studio's own `--estimate-only` guardrail agrees it fits (13.43 GiB at 16384, 14.39 at 24576, 15.36 at 32768 against a 16,376 MiB card).

**Two corrections the record needs, both expensive if left.** (a) **The GPUs were recorded backwards.** The verifier model runs on **GPU0**, the
RTX A4000 (16,376 MiB) — unloading it dropped GPU0 from 12,648 MiB to 59 MiB. The 22.9 GiB on GPU1, the RTX 3090, is the **local** model, and
that is not LM Studio at all: it is a separate process, `strata --serve --pack …/iq3_s --native Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S… --max-context 204800 --kv int8`
(`/v1/models` reports `"gpus":[1]`). Any plan that spends "the free space on GPU1" is spending the local model's card. (b) **`compact` is broken
independently of the window.** `cli.mjs compact qa "…"` returns `{"ok":false,"error":"compact: no compaction entry was written for seat qa (task 275369)"}`
at a now-ample 16384, with no entry in `log qa`; "compaction needs the same window" no longer explains it.

**What the raise bought, measured, and where it stops.** With the window fixed and a no-handoff reset, `qa` WAKED and worked: it planned
(`stopReason=toolUse`), read `src/shellregistry.mjs` (8,754 chars) and `src/seattools.mjs` (16,505 chars), and was then cut mid-review at
`in=14184 out=1 stopReason=length`. So a whole-file review of #4849 does not fit in any window this box can currently serve, and the binding
rule (#4866: a seat without an oracle may author, may not close) still has no reachable verifier. **`#4849 remains UNVERIFIED and `claimed`;
nothing landed.** The decision now on the operator is a host-capacity one: 24,576 tokens costs ~1.1 GiB more KV on the A4000 (measured headroom
~2.4 GiB, LM Studio estimate 14.39 GiB of 16,376 MiB — tight), or the delegate pre-chunks review briefs so each leg fits an existing window.

**Operating acts the delegate took, with their warrant.** Two `reset` writes on `qa` — first with a handoff (which is what produced the
`system, user, user` payload and is now part of DEFECT 1's evidence), then without one — both via the product's own
`cli.mjs reset <seat> [handoff] [--dry-run]`, whose `--dry-run` was run first and reported `writes: 0`. A reset **writes a boundary and keeps
the transcript**; `docs/runbooks/degeneration-guard.md` is the entry point for a degenerate seat and D78 is the reason a reset is never casual.
`qa2` and `auditor` carry the same residue (189 and 158 unanswered user turns) and were deliberately **left alone** — three verifier-family
seats reset in one session is a rig-level call, not a delegate's.

**Insurance minted, because the change was one sweep from unrecoverable.** `src/shellregistry.mjs` was **untracked** and its blob existed
nowhere in the object database (`git hash-object` then `git cat-file -e` → absent); the only copy outside the detached worktree was under
gitignored `.spike/`. All five #4849 files are now blob refs `refs/rescued/impl-4849-{shellregistry.mjs, seattools.mjs, seatguard.mjs,
seattools.test.mjs, seatguard.test.mjs}`, each round-tripped byte-identical to the file in the tree. That is anti-sweep insurance, **not**
evidence about the change — read the files in the worktree (the standing rule against citing machine-local git objects as durable evidence,
ROADMAP 190, still holds).

**Tree-shape fixes, granted by the operator as "fix the inconsistency".** `/home/chexxor/Git/durian-dev/seatroot` moved off detached HEAD onto
branch **`seatroot/linux`** at the same commit (no commit moved; the 5 uncommitted files untouched) and received a gitignored
`durig.config.json` — deliberately carrying the **absolute** `DURIG_DB` path so an instrument run there measures this rig rather than silently

(was `seat "pm" points at local/iq3_s, but no "local" provider is configured`) and `demo/clockin-digest.test.mjs` (was `Command failed:
git rev-list --count main..(no branch)`) now exit 0. Suite control, both trees, with `DURIG_DB` pinned to a scratch store so no demo can touch
the operator's store: **seat root 237 PASS / 1 FAIL, live checkout the same single FAIL** — `demo/deepinfra-catalog.test.mjs`
(`seat "qa" names verifier/mistralai/ministral-3-14b-reasoning, which is not in the fallback catalog — it would resolve to no_model`),
identical in both trees. The main-4 / seat-root-3 divergence D173 carried is now **zero**, and no failure is attributable to #4849.

**What was routed, and to whom.** A findings brief went to **pm** (`.spike/fix-20261030/send-pm-findings.md`) asking the decomposition owner —
not the delegate — to mint rows for the role-sequence defect, the `compact` defect, and ROADMAP **208**, which still prints `NO ROW 208` in
`tools/roadmap-queue-coverage.mjs` despite being a live measured constraint. The operator still holds the research prompt

## D175 — the alternation rule is the provider template's, not "consecutive user turns"; auto-compaction is dead by construction on a small window; the A4000 spend (delegate, 2026-10-30, Linux)

> **CORRECTED BY D176 — the middle clause of this heading is false.** Auto-compaction is not unavailable on a small
> window; it is available only near the ceiling, where the summary it writes keeps the newest 20,000 tokens anyway and
> the turn dies anyway. Measured the same night (`qa`, entries 275457 / 275459). Read D176 before quoting this heading
> as policy.

**The instrument I wrote on this grant was wrong in the way that matters, and the rig showed it immediately.** The operator asked for the
"render the outgoing conversation shape" diagnostic (my own next-session improvement #1). I wrote `tools/seat-turn-shape.mjs` with a
*plausible* predicate — "two consecutive `user` roles" — and it **cleared a `qa` turn that then failed**: the request died at a 24,576-token
window with `stopReason=error`, `input=0`, and the template's 500. So the predicate was replaced with the template's literal rule, read from
LM Studio's generated file (`.lmstudio/.internal/temp/lmstudio-chat-template-OrONg3/chat-template.jinja`, block *"Checks for alternating
user/assistant messages."*, `raise_exception` at line 48):

```jinja
{%- if message.role == 'user' or (message.role == 'assistant' and message.tool_calls | length == 0) %}
    {%- if (message['role'] == 'user') != (ns.index % 2 == 0) %} raise_exception(...)
```

The projection that must alternate is **every `user` plus every `assistant` that carries NO tool calls**, from index 0 as
`user, assistant, user, …`. Therefore **a tool-calling assistant does not satisfy the alternation** and a tool result is never counted:
a seat resuming after a tool-calling turn is in the wrong slot the moment anything appends a user turn. That is the real shape of #4886,
sharper than D174's "consecutive user turns", and it explains why the failure reappeared after a *successful* tool-using turn.
**The lesson to keep: an instrument that encodes your guess about a contract, instead of the contract, is worse than no instrument — it
buys confidence.** The fixture now pins the exact rule (`demo/seat-turn-shape.test.mjs`: a tool-calling assistant must NOT enter the
projection; a tool result is uncounted; the first counted message must be `user`; an empty assistant with no tool calls IS counted).

**RED→GREEN for the instrument, in the field.** Read straight off the store through `replayView` + `storage.scanEntries`: immediately before
the failed attempt it said `next send: AT RISK` (correct), and after a bare `cli.mjs reset qa` (no handoff — the handoff is itself a user
turn) it said `window 0 messages … next send: ADMISSIBLE`, which is what gated the retry. Measured across the 12 seats at that moment:
**6 windows already carried a parity break and 11 of 12 seats would be refused on their next `send`** — including the healthy local ones,
whose provider tolerates it. That is a rig-level fact for #4886, not a qa fact.

**A `compact` that completes and writes nothing is a documented no-op, not a failure — and on this window auto-compaction can never fire.**
Read from the shipped dependency: the task's `select` phase does `const cut = selectCut(view, policy.keepRecentTokens)` and
**`if (cut === undefined) return complete(...)`** (`vendor/pi-main/.../harness/compaction.js:69-71`); `selectCut` returns `undefined` when
walking back never accumulates `keepRecentTokens` tokens (`compaction.js:211-234`). durian-pi passes **no** compaction policy — the only
harness setting is `settings: streamSettings(CFG)` (`cli.mjs:414-423`, and `streamSettings` returns `stream.timeoutMs` alone,
`src/config.mjs:246-259`) — so every seat runs `DEFAULT_COMPACTION_POLICY`: `reserveTokens 16384, keepRecentTokens 20000,
backgroundTokens 32768` (`harness/agent.js:10-15`). Against a 24,576 window: blocking = 8,192, background = **−24,576 (impossible)**, and
`thresholdCompaction` refuses to start unless `selectCut` finds a cut (`generation.js:236-245`) — which needs >20,000 tokens kept, i.e.
within ~4,500 tokens of the ceiling. And the summary request would be `min(0.8·16384, model.maxTokens)` = up to **13,107 tokens, larger than
the window compaction exists to protect**. So `cli.mjs:1344`'s `no compaction entry was written` was reporting a legitimate no-op as a
defect, at both 16,384 and 24,576 — which retires the "compaction needs the same window" theory for good.
**Recommendation offered to the operator (not decided, not built; carrier row #4887, `impl`):** feed pi-durable's existing
`modelOverrides` seam (`compaction.js:194-201`) from new `DURIG_COMPACTION_*` keys via a `compactionSettings(CFG)` next to `streamSettings`,
one call site at `cli.mjs:414-423`; verifier class `reserveTokens 4096 / keepRecentTokens 8192 / backgroundTokens 8192` (blocking 20,480,
background 12,288, summary capped at 3,000); **leave the local class on defaults** (coherent at 200,000); and split the reporting into
`NO-OP / FAILED (<compactionFailure>) / COMPACTED (<entry id>)` with distinct exit codes, printing the seat's token count against the
policy. `contextConsumption` (`src/context.mjs:104`) already computes the "will there be anything to cut?" answer, before spending the verb.

**Capacity, spent on the operator's grant and measured.** `lms load … -c 24576 --parallel 1 --gpu max`: GPU0 15,202/16,376 MiB, and a
**21,135-token** request completed in **19.1 s** (at 8,192 that same size was refused; at 16,384 a review was cut at `in=14184`). LM Studio's
`--estimate-only` said 14.39 GiB where 14.85 GiB loaded — **the estimate runs ~0.35 GiB low**, so budget against measurement. `lms` is the
only write surface: the app's `:1234` REST exposes `GET /api/v0/models` only. **LM Studio restores `--ctx-size 8192 --parallel 4` on app
relaunch**, so the three-way re-check (API / server cmdline / a request at the real size) belongs after every restart.

**Landed this session (all cited, all staged):** `tools/seat-turn-shape.mjs` + `demo/seat-turn-shape.test.mjs` (read-only, exits 1 on an
unreadable store, `--strict` for a gate); `docs/runbooks/verifier-serving-headroom.md` (front-matter conformant; indexed in
`docs/runbooks/README.md` twice) carrying the KV cost formula from the model file's own metadata (**160 KiB/token**: 40 layers × 8 KV heads ×
(128+128) × 2 B), the ctx→GiB table, the GPU ownership correction, the vendor-tool procedure with a captured restore recipe, and the
**briefing arithmetic** — one batched brief per seat per session (measured: a 21k-token verifier completion = 19 s; a 162k-token local seat
turn = 12–15 min), name the claims and cap the files, demand the verdict before the reading, and never re-send a failed brief because it is
a deposit, not a retry. Plus new sections in `docs/runbooks/compact-a-seat.md` (the no-op mechanism and the recommended policy, labelled
RECOMMENDED pending the operator). Suite-relevant checks run green: `demo/seat-turn-shape.test.mjs`, `demo/format.test.mjs`,
`demo/runbook-frontmatter.test.mjs`, `tools/doc-integrity-guard.mjs` (41 runbooks, 0 hard).

## D176 — auto-compaction is not "dead" on a small window, it is a trap that fires at the ceiling; a `done` verify row can cite lines that point nowhere; and the operator's acceptance was not converted into a ruling the operator had not given (delegate, 2026-10-30, Linux)

**Correction to D175, in D175's own heading.** D175 recorded "auto-compaction is dead by construction on a small
window." That is **false as stated**, and the rig produced the counter-example the same night: on `qa`'s verifier leg
(window 24,576) a turn went out at `input=17,445`, the next request crossed `selectCut`'s `keepRecentTokens = 20,000`
budget, a **real `pi.compaction` entry was written (275457)**, and the turn after it came back
**`input=20,109, output=1, stopReason=length` with an empty reply (275459)**. The arithmetic that made D175 look right
is real — `background = (window − reserveTokens) − backgroundTokens = 8,192 − 32,768 = −24,576`, so the background tier
can never fire — but `blocking` fires at 8,192 and `selectCut` only refuses *below* 20,000 accumulated tokens. So on a
24,576 window auto-compaction is **not unavailable; it is available only in the last ~4,500 tokens, and by then the
summary it writes keeps the newest 20,000 tokens anyway, which is the whole window.** That is a worse failure than the
no-op D175 described: a no-op misleads, this one **destroys a turn that was about to produce a verdict**. The wording in
`docs/runbooks/compact-a-seat.md` is corrected to that effect with these entry ids as evidence.
**Why it matters beyond the wording:** it changes the status of the #4887 recommendation. The proposed values
(`reserveTokens 4096`, `keepRecentTokens 8192`, `backgroundTokens 8192`) are not a tidy-up — with them background fires
at 12,288 *while there is room to answer*, which is the only configuration in which a verifier leg on this window
completes reliably. Tonight's single successful leg completed **only because the delegate bounded the reading by hand**
(`src/seatguard.mjs` is 26,532 chars; reading it whole is what pushed the request into the band).

**A `done` verify row is not a verified claim: the substance and its citations can come apart, and the instrument that
exists does not see the gap.** `qa2` completed #4891 (`stopReason=stop`) with PROCEED on C3 — the guard's set is
*derived*, `export const SHELL_TOOLS = new Set(shellToolNames())` — which my own independent read corroborates
(`shellToolNames()` maps `SHELL_CANDIDATES`, `src/shellregistry.mjs:106-107`). But its citations do not resolve: it
placed `SHELL_TOOLS` at `seatguard.mjs:350-354` (it is at **`:144`**; 348–356 is an unrelated control-plane comment),
the registry import at **line 20** (it is **`:22`**), and `SHELL_CANDIDATES` at **lines 20–30** (they are at **`:79`**).
`node tools/review-cite-check.mjs` on the dumped summary returns **exit 0 with `pathCites 1/0`** — it validates that a
path exists and that a range fits inside the file, never that the cited lines contain the cited symbol. D162 said
citation integrity is a machine check, not a reading habit; this is the next step that claim implies: **the check needs
to bind a citation to the symbol it names**, or a verifier that satisfies P1 Grounding's *shape* still reports evidence
that does not exist. No row owns that yet — it is pm's to mint, and qa2's own report row **#4897** is in front of pm.

**The delegate did not turn the operator's "I accept your recommendations" into a ruling the operator had not
specifically given.** Row #4887's release was the one thing labelled *RECOMMENDED — the operator has not ruled*, and its
body predated the mechanism. Writing an attributed ruling into the store — through `pm`, who then holds it, releases
it, and directs `impl` by it — is the kind of act that gets load-bearing in one round trip and costs a retraction plus a
wrong seat-build to undo. So the grant was **asked about, not inferred**, and the pointer now names it as an open
operator decision. The contrast that makes this the right call: where the operator *had* granted capacity (grant 12),
the delegate spent it and reported the measurement; the difference is specificity, not caution.

**Two deliberate non-acts, both grounded.** (1) The delegate did **not** re-drive `qa`'s #4890 after it died: its
post-compaction context is already ~20,109 tokens, so another send re-triggers the same cut, and re-sending a brief is a
deposit not a retry (the store keeps the user turn and the empty assistant turn). (2) The delegate did **not** raise the
verifier slot this session even though ~1,160 MiB (~4,096 tokens at 160 KiB/token) is free on GPU0, because tonight's
failure is a **policy** defect, not a size defect — raising the window moves the band, it does not remove it. Recorded
so the next session does not read the free space as an invitation.

**The completion reset is still live, and this time it moved a seat onto the live checkout.** `qa2`'s `complete_work`
re-pointed its persisted cwd to the serving process's cwd — `/home/chexxor/Git/Durian-Pi` — so pm, lead **and qa2** were
off the operator-approved root (#4882's mechanism, self-worsening per closed item, exactly as that row says). The
delegate repaired it under grant 11: `up rig.selfdev.json --refresh --dry-run` named all three
(`from: /home/chexxor/Git/Durian-Pi → to: /home/chexxor/Git/durian-dev/seatroot`), the refresh applied, the re-dry-run
shows `changes: {}` for all 12 seats, and the worktree/branch inventories diffed unchanged with `refs/rescued` still 489.
**The habit to keep: run `send` from the approved root, and re-check seat drift with `up … --refresh --dry-run` (a
read-only verb that names every pending re-point) before the next writing verb** — because the F12 guard
(`cli.mjs:466`) fails closed in whichever direction the persisted cwd currently disagrees.

**What pm's rulings looked like when pm's own turn errored:** `send pm` settled `unanswered / model_error` with
`stopReason: toolUse`, yet the queue records what pm decided — **#4890 and #4891 released to `queued`**, and **#4894**
(commit the 5 files *before* completing, because #4882 can strand them), **#4895** (`rig-portability-audit.mjs` gives
different findings from the seat root than from the live checkout, so the gate depends on where you stood), **#4896**
(`seat-turn-shape.mjs` as pre-flight and as #4886's fixture source; the 6/12 parity break is its own concern).
**A turn that errors after a tool call still committed that call**: the model_error is the *reply*'s failure, not the
act's. Read the queue, not the transcript, to find out what a seat decided.

**Evidence:** `send pm` out `.spike/fix-20261031/send-pm-verdict-out.json`; queue diffs

## D177 — a seat at its context ceiling cannot be repaired by `compact`, because compaction IS a summarization call and fails for the same reason the turn did; an operator ruling reaches the team only as a seat's row, and only sender/recipient may release; and the delegate's own session died of host memory pressure (delegate, 2026-10-30, Linux)

**Decision.** (1) The operator's ruling — **"Yes, I authorize those actions"** (19:1xZ), covering the #4887
compaction-config build, raising #4886's priority, and spending no further verifier capacity — was **conveyed to a
seat and recorded as grants 13–15**, and the delegate deliberately did **not** enact any part of it by hand. It
travelled as **lead's rows #4898/#4899**, not as a delegate write. (2) The delegate stopped trying to reach `pm`
after one failed send and stopped trying to repair it after `compact` failed, and instead **escalated the ceiling**
rather than reaching for `reset` on a seat whose routing history is load-bearing. (3) Every seat run launched from
now on is **detached with `setsid`**, and host RAM is pre-flighted before the 441 MB store is touched.

**Why (1) — the rig has no path from an operator to a held row except through a party to it.** `pm` holds #4887 and
was unreachable, and lead's own prior measurement (**#4867**) is that **only sender or recipient may release**, while
`revise_work` edits subject/body only and cannot fix a `held` row's body or tier. So the only lawful route was
**lead → impl (#4898, `queued`)** instructing the **recipient** to `release_work(4887)`. This is also why the ruling
must not be recorded as "done": **#4886's tier is still `feature` and still `held by pm`** — lead ruled the priority
in prose and could not set it. A ruling is not an act; the row is the act.

**Why (2) — `compact` cannot save a seat at its ceiling, and the failure is the same failure.** `status` names it for
`pm` (context **184,507/200,000 = 0.9225**): **`Compaction failed: Summarization hit the token limit; the summary is
incomplete`**, `settledReason: model_error`, and the turn recorded **no assistant entry at all** (entry 275487 is a bare
user turn). Then `compact qa2 --dry-run` failed the same way at **18,453 of 24,576** — so #4876 ("`compact` returns
`no compaction entry was written`") reproduces on a **small** seat too, and D176's reading is now sharpened:
**compaction needs headroom to summarize, not just to fire.** That single fact is the strongest argument yet for the
#4887 values, and it retires `compact` from the delegate's list of repairs, leaving only `reset` (#4886) — amnesia.

**Why (3) — the delegate's own harness died mid-act and took the seat run with it.** `nohup … &` detaches from the
terminal, not from the harness's process group; when the harness died, lead's submission 275494 was left `placed` and
`send-lead-out.json` stayed empty. Re-arm instruments: **`resume`/`doctor` CANCELS a `placed` run, it does not retry
it** (`cli.mjs:1101-1112`), and **`cli.mjs <verb> --help` RUNS THE VERB** — the delegate's `doctor --help` performed a
real cancel (benign, intended in the following deliberate call, recorded as an unintended write). The brief itself
survived as entry **275493**, so the fix was a **short nudge** (a ~60-token deposit) rather than a re-send of the whole
findings file; lead then answered `stopReason=stop`. Host cause is **UNVERIFIED but bounded**: 7 kernel OOM kills in
this user's slice, `user.slice memory.peak 96.1 GB` against `MemTotal 98,780,144 kB`, swap 62 % used, `strata-host`
50.6 GB RSS, and **no core dump in the crash window** (SIGKILL leaves none, whereas this box does core node SIGABRTs).
Full record: `docs/incidents/2026-10-30-delegate-session-lost-to-host-memory-pressure.md`.

**Evidence.** `status` `latestByConv["3"]` (pm: `unanswered`/`model_error` + the compaction detail) and
`context.pm` (184,507/200,000); `compact --dry-run` failures as tasks **275491** (pm) and **275492** (qa2); queue
verification `.spike/fix-20261031/queue-after-lead2.json` → census **4,899 = 3,757 done / 780 cancelled / 321 held /
22 queued / 17 deferred / 2 claimed (#4849 impl, #4890 qa)**, new **#4898** (lead→impl, `queued` 20:08:39.757Z) and
**#4899** (lead→devtools, `held` 20:08:39.766Z), **#4886 still `held`, tier `feature`**; lead's answer at entry
**275506** and `.spike/fix-20261031/send-lead-nudge-out.json` (`settledStatus: done`, `stopReason: stop`); session
JSONL gap `19:56:54.590Z → 19:59:02.199Z`; `coredumpctl list --since '2026-10-30 14:50'` → none, vs cores at

## D178 — a seat cannot commit its own verified work on this host (there is no seat shell on Linux), so the delegate INSURED the work rather than committing it or dogfooding the unlanded fix; and `up … --refresh --dry-run` printing `changes: {}` is a VACUOUS pass about the seat root (delegate, 2026-10-30, Linux)

**Decision.** Two acts, both chosen against a tempting alternative:

1. **Insure, do not impersonate, and do not dogfood the unlanded fix.** The five files of #4849 (ROADMAP 217,
   authored by seat `impl`, cross-family verified) sat UNCOMMITTED in the approved seat root. The delegate captured
   them as a patch plus verbatim copies with sha256sums and a manifest, and left the commit to a ruling — rather than
   (a) committing them itself, or (b) serving `impl` from the seat root so its own new code would give it a shell.
2. **Stop citing `up … --refresh --dry-run` → `changes: {}` as evidence about the seat root.** It is vacuous in this
   rig's configuration. The honest read is the newest `pi.agent` document revision in the store.

**Why (1) — the order the team is operating under is inenactable by its recipient, and the reason is the item's own
defect.** pm's addendum **#4894** tells `impl` to commit its five files *before* completing #4849, because
`complete_work` can re-point a seat's persisted cwd (#4882) and strand them. Measured on this host, **no seat has a
shell at all** in the landed code: `src/seattools.mjs:214-222` reads "`bash` is deliberately absent … the seat shell is
PowerShell" and registers `shell: createPowerShellTool()`, which resolves `pwsh` then `powershell`; neither exists here
(`bash` does). `tools/rig-portability-audit.mjs` states the consequence in its own words: *"every seat shell call is a
spawn error: **no git, no demo suite, and completions are self-declared**"*. So the fix for "a seat cannot run git" is
itself the thing that would let the seat run git — a dependency inversion that will recur on every landing until 217
lands, and the reason #4849's own author could not protect its own work.

Both available shortcuts were rejected for named reasons, not deference:

- **Committing on the seat's behalf** is arguably inside grant 11 (tree-shape acts on the approved seat root), but
  #4849 is `claimed`: the delegate would be authoring a commit into another actor's in-flight item and pre-empting the
  three landing gates in `docs/BRANCH-AND-WORKTREE-LIFECYCLE.md`. Insurance removes the loss hazard, which was the
  actual worry, without touching attribution.
- **Serving `impl` from the seat root** would have run its own uncommitted code as the harness. Measured at code level
  (read-only import, no harness, no store): `shellToolNames()` → `["powershell","bash"]`, `selectSeatShell()` →
  `{"name":"bash","degraded":false}` with `canStart: true`, and `programOnPath("bash")` → `/usr/bin/bash`. So it would
  very likely have worked — and it is still the wrong call, because the runtime half of that mechanism is exactly what
  the queue is waiting to land and what qa2 abstained from (`OUT-OF-SCOPE-NEEDS-RUNTIME-PROOF`: the 22 `spawn … ENOENT`
  arms, `bash` permitted at execution time). Promoting unverified code to the serving harness to make a commit
  convenient would manufacture the evidence instead of earning it. Both paths are now a ruling for **lead or the
  operator**, and the delegate said so in the wake brief.

**Why (2) — the pass had no comparison in it.** D177 recorded "12 seats, `changes: {}`" as proof the root was repaired.
But the refresh target is `seat.cwd ?? spec.cwd ?? CFG.DURIG_SEAT_ROOT` (`cli.mjs:679`, `cli.mjs:794`), and
`rig.selfdev.json` declares **no** cwd for any seat (grep: 0 occurrences of the root path in the rig file). With
`DURIG_SEAT_ROOT` unset, all three operands are undefined, so every seat prints `changes: {}` no matter where it
actually points. Reading the store instead: 12 seats on `/home/chexxor/Git/durian-dev/seatroot` (so D177's conclusion
was right, its evidence was not), **plus a 13th `pi.agent` document — doc 216675, revision 2263478 — still at
`C:\Users\Alex\dsh-Projects\pi-opendurig`**. That is an orphan conversation, not one of the 12 roster seats, which is
why it never trips the F12 guard (the guard iterates the roster) and why it has survived every `--refresh`: a leaked
root that no instrument names. Also false on this build: `docs/SELFDEV.md` still claims `ps`/`status` show each seat's
`root` (#261) — `status.seats[]` carries no such field.

**A third thing this exposed, because it silently costs turns.** Rows that send a seat to a doc section must account for
the seat's branch lag: `seatroot/linux` is **13 commits behind `main`** (`git rev-list --count seatroot/linux..main` =
13, measured 2026-10-31; an earlier note in this file said 8 — recount before you act on a lag number), and #4898 pointed `impl` at
`docs/runbooks/compact-a-seat.md` §"What auto-compaction is configured to, and what to set it to" — text that exists
only on `main`. The delegate inlined the operator-approved values into the brief and re-verified the code anchors **in
the seat's own tree** rather than quoting main's line numbers (`src/config.mjs:246`, `cli.mjs:414`/`:423`,
`cli.mjs:1344` all match in that tree by luck, not by construction).

**What this changes for the next delegate.** Pre-flight the root by reading the newest `pi.agent` revision, not by a
dry-run; run `send` with **cwd = the approved seat root** (that is what causes the #4882 re-point in the first place —
D177's drift came from serving from the live checkout) and with `DURIG_SEAT_ROOT` set so the F12 guard is live; and
when a plan depends on a seat running `git`, `node`, or any shell verb, treat it as blocked until 217 lands and route
the measurement through the #4858 delegate-run carve-out instead.

**Evidence.** `src/seattools.mjs:214-222` and `src/seatguard.mjs:122` (`SHELL_TOOLS = new Set(["bash","powershell"])` —
the *guard* allows bash, the *tool* is PowerShell-only); `tools/rig-portability-audit.mjs` → "NOT PORTABLE ON THIS
HOST — 2 finding(s)", findings `seat-shell-availability` and `seat-host-unaware`, cost 581 ms; insurance at
`.spike/fix-20261101/insurance-4849/` (manifest naming tree/branch/HEAD `3860e5d1`, `patch-4849-tracked.diff` 245
lines sha256 `c7e1afb1…`, `files/shellregistry.mjs` 8,793 B sha256 `8e5476f6…`, plus the four modified files);
delegate-run suites in the seat root, `node demo/seatguard.test.mjs` exit 0 "PASS — the guard holds" and
`node demo/seattools.test.mjs` exit 0 "PASS — the controls are wired" (exit codes read directly, never through a pipe);
`node .spike/fix-20261101/read-cwd4.mjs` for the roots; `tools/channel-preflight.mjs` → 22 claimable rows, broker down,
`placed=0 queued=0`, "the wedge does NOT survive a restart"; `durig.config.json` in the seat root pins
`DURIG_DB=/home/chexxor/Git/Durian-Pi/selfdev.sqlite`, `local` = `http://127.0.0.1:47831/v1` `iq3_s` ctx 200000,
`verifier` = `http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1` `ministral-3-14b-reasoning` ctx 24576 max 3000; `rig.selfdev.json` models are
`local/iq3_s` and `verifier/…` — the `rig.selfdev.json`-vs-docs model mismatch is why `SELFDEV.md` tells you to
re-derive the seat table rather than read it.


**Outcome (recorded after the decision was written, because it changed the decision's meaning).** The one wake
(`send impl`, request id `d178-impl-4849-4887`, cwd = the approved seat root, `DURIG_SEAT_ROOT` set, store backed up to
`.spike/fix-20261101/store-backup-pre-send-20261030-161115.sqlite` first) settled `done` / `stopReason: stop` and moved
three rows: **#4849 `done`**, **#4898 `done`**, **#4887 released to `queued`** for the next owner. The seat performed
BOTH acts pm attached to the withdrawn #4894 — so "a seat cannot act without a shell" was too strong: `claim`,
`complete` and `prepare_workspace` are rig tools, not shell verbs. What the missing shell costs is exactly `git`: the
seat used `prepare_workspace`, which created a **new locked worktree + branch `item-4898` off the seat root's HEAD
`3860e5d1`**, and its commit act is now a ruling for someone who can run `git` — the same blocker from the other side.
Delegate-run verification of that build: `node --check` ×3 exit 0, `demo/config.test.mjs` exit 0 including a new
COMPACTION POLICY section (the 2 `DURIG_MODEL_*` regressions D177 predicted did NOT fire), full sweep 2 RED both
attributed by the #4895 method. **Two findings routed, not fixed:** the seat's report claimed there is no `CONFIG_KEYS`
list and that `node_modules` is absent in its own worktree — both false in the tree it was working in (`CONFIG_KEYS` at
`src/config.mjs:111`; `node_modules` present with `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent` 3.1.6 and 2.8.3), and the five new
`DURIG_COMPACTION_*` keys (`ENABLED`, `MODEL_OVERRIDES`, `RESERVE_TOKENS`, `KEEP_RECENT_TOKENS`, `BACKGROUND_TOKENS`) are
**not** registered in it. **Durable lesson, generalized:** a fresh worktree carries no
gitignored `durig.config.json`, so a whole-suite sweep run inside one manufactures a **FALSE RED** —
`demo/local-model-pointer.test.mjs` is exit 1 in `item-4898` (no `local` provider configured) and exit 0 in the seat
root. Attribute every RED to a tree before calling it a regression.

**Clock-out note (D178): what cost wall-clock, and what would shorten the next one.** (1) **The 200-line pointer cap is
now the dominant cost of a clock-out** — ~40 min went to re-compressing `docs/NEXT.md` from 213 to 199 lines because the
pointer had grown past the cap mid-session and every new fact displaced another. The cap is right (a 4,724-line pointer
overflowed a 50 KB read cap into 8 chunked reads — see the comment in `demo/next-pointer.test.mjs`), but the *act* it
demands is mechanical: a seat should own it. Proposed row for pm/devtools: a `tools/pointer-fit.mjs` that prints the
per-paragraph line counts and the archive-append command with the `sed -n "s,e p"` proof filled in, so the next delegate
spends judgement on what to cut, not on `wc -l` loops. (2) **Two measurements I re-derived by hand this session are now
one command each** — `.spike/fix-20261101/rows.mjs` prints the row state, the parked-on-pm set, and the reachability map
from `queue --json` / `status --json`; promote it to `tools/` if the team accepts the finding that `status.attention`
under-reports over-window seats. (3) **Wake yield, measured:** the queue sat ~1.5 h with zero movement because no seat
was awake; one `send` moved 3 rows and cleared 2 acts in ~20 min of wall clock (21:14:31 → 21:31:09). A brief that
carries TWO items plus their release instruction, with the approved values inlined (branch lag makes doc-section anchors
unusable), roughly doubles what one wake returns. (4) **A fresh worktree costs a false RED** unless the gitignored
`durig.config.json` is copied or the sweep is attributed per tree — check for that file before believing any suite RED.

## D179 — a landing ruling has a *sequencing* consequence the options did not state: committing the change is what makes the author's own proof possible; and "the seat has no shell" turned out to be two different blockers (delegate, 2026-10-31, Linux)

**What the operator granted.** Given the three options in D178, the operator said to proceed and finish. The delegate read
that as: execute **(b)** first (it is the only path that can produce the runtime evidence the team has been refusing to
fake), then **(a)** for whatever the seat cannot close, with **(c)** as the honest residue if the proof fails — *report the
unverified half rather than paper over it.*

**Executed, with shas.** `(a)` — `seatroot/linux` **`f8840349`** = #4849/ROADMAP 217 (5 files, 273 insertions, new
`src/shellregistry.mjs`); branch `item-4898` **`9beb1ae3`** = #4887/#4898 (3 files, 310 insertions). Both committed with
explicit paths, nothing pushed, no merge, `main` untouched, both insurances re-verified byte-identical first. `(b)` — two
detached wakes served **from the seat root itself**, so the seat root's own code was the harness.

**What (b) actually measured, and why the answer is better than the proof I asked for.** The seat's shell call **reached
a tool named `bash`** and was refused by the *degraded-cwd* rule: "your seat cwd IS the SHARED checkout … call
`prepare_workspace` first … Refused as a `bash` call; the seat shell registered on this host is `bash`". That refusal text
is 217's own wording, evaluated live from the tree carrying it — so **registration and selection are proven at runtime**,
which is strictly more than D178 had. The execution half is still unproven, for a reason nobody had named: the second
wake's `prepare_workspace` failed with `no claimed item #4902 is yours; call claim_work first`. So the chain to a
seat-executed acceptance is: *claimed row → worktree forked from a ref that carries the change → shell allowed there*.
The seat correctly refused to hand-create a worktree (its acceptance would then test the wrong tree) and refused to run
the suite in a fork that lacked its files.

**The circularity, and what breaks it.** No shell → cannot commit; no commit → no ref to fork → cannot get a worktree →
cannot get a shell. The delegate's grant-11 commit is the thing that breaks the loop, and that is the part of the ruling
worth keeping: it was not "the delegate does the seat's work", it was *supplying the missing ref*. The remaining act is a
seat act and stays one: a fresh row addressed to `impl` (`lead -> impl` is a permitted edge) that `impl` can claim, with
`prepare_workspace` given that explicit itemId — because the default re-attaches to the most recently claimed item, whose
worktree was the **delegate's `item-4898`**.

**Keeping a carve-out honest.** The seat authored its own commit-message file with the file tool (not the shell) and left
the exit codes as literal `EXIT=__` with the rule: *"Do not commit this message with the placeholders filled by anyone who
did not run the commands in this tree."* The delegate then ran them in that tree (`node --check` ×3 exit 0;
`demo/seatguard.test.mjs` exit 0 "PASS — the guard holds"; `demo/seattools.test.mjs` exit 0 "PASS — the controls are
wired"), filled the placeholders from that run, and appended a RUNNER block naming the delegate, the OS, the tree state
(`3860e5d1` + the then-uncommitted files) and what remains unverified. **A carve-out that does not name its runner is a
fake oracle wearing real evidence.**

**Two findings the delegate routed rather than fixed.** (1) **Org edge vs. store:** `rig.selfdev.json` gives
`impl maySendTo: pm, qa, auditor, advocate, designer, scribe, devtools, security, architect, qa2` — `lead` absent — yet the
store holds **27 rows with `from=impl, to=lead`** (#42 … #4901). `impl` was refused when told to report to `lead` and
redirected to `devtools` (#4902, #4903). The delegate's own brief had made that mistake; the seat caught it. (2) The
`rig.selfdev.json` instruction text still says "The shell tool is powershell, all lowercase" for 1 of 12 seats — after
`f8840349` the name is host-conditional (`bash` on Linux), so the exact-names block is now a lie about this host.

**Still open after this decision (do not read "committed" as "landed"):** neither change set is on `main`; the merge
topology is `lead`'s ruling under the merge runbook; 217's execution half, all win32 paths, and the 22 ENOENT arms remain
unverified; the five `DURIG_COMPACTION_*` keys are still unregistered in `CONFIG_KEYS` (`src/config.mjs:111`).

**Clock-out note (D179): what cost wall-clock, and what would shorten the next one.** (1) **Three wakes, three different
refusals, and each refusal cost a measurement cycle to interpret.** 217's execution proof failed twice for reasons that
were *not* the defect under test — first the degraded-cwd guard, then `prepare_workspace`'s "no claimed item #4902 is
yours". Both are correct behaviours, and both read like failures of the change. Proposed seat act, cheap and high-value:
have the refusal text name the **next verb** ("claim a row, then `prepare_workspace(itemId)`"), which it already partly
does — and have `prepare_workspace`'s error name the *itemId you passed vs the one you hold*. (2) **The pointer cap again
dominated clock-out**: this session's head rewrite was ~35 min for the same mechanical reason as D178 (facts displacing
facts under `wc -l`). The `tools/pointer-fit.mjs` proposal in the D178 note is now proven twice; promote it. (3) **A
stale-base hazard is now measurable at fork time and nobody measures it.** Every new item worktree forks from the ref the
seat root's cwd points at — tonight `f8840349`, **14 commits behind `main`** — so a seat can silently implement against an
old tree while the pointer/runbooks it reads are newer. Proposed instrument (devtools-scope): print
`base_lag = git rev-list --count <base>..main` in `prepare_workspace`'s JSON and stamp the base sha on the branch, so a
stale fork is visible at creation instead of at review. (4) **A seat's persisted cwd following its own item worktree
breaks the wake channel for everyone else** — the root-drift guard refused the delegate's next `send` because `impl`'s cwd
had moved to an unlocked `item-4904`. One row for devtools on whether settle should reset cwd, `prepare_workspace` should
lock what it creates, or the guard should scope to the seat being woken.

## D180 — `DURIG_SEAT_ROOT` is not only a guard input, it is the **root selector**; unsetting it to get past a drift refusal re-points the seat at a different checkout

**Decision (2026-10-31, delegate, `label-withheld-per-D205` / Linux):** the next delegate must treat "unset
`DURIG_SEAT_ROOT`" as a **workspace write**, not as relaxing a check. I did it to get a wake through and it silently
moved a seat from the approved root into the delegate's own repo.

**What happened, in order, with the numbers.** (1) A wake to `devtools` under `DURIG_SEAT_ROOT` was **refused** by the
root-drift guard: `seat "impl" is pointed at a different worktree than DURIG_SEAT_ROOT: persisted cwd
"/home/chexxor/Git/durian-dev/seatroot/item-4904" vs DURIG_SEAT_ROOT "/home/chexxor/Git/durian-dev/seatroot"`. Note the
shape of that failure: **an unrelated seat's** cwd drift (`impl`, left in an **unlocked** `item-4904` by #4904's
`prepare_workspace`) blocked a send **to a different seat**. (2) I "fixed" it the way the error text told me — *or unset
`DURIG_SEAT_ROOT`* — and sent. (3) Measured after the run: **`devtools`'s newest `pi.agent` revision (doc 4935 = conv
4930, docs map conv+5) reads `cwd=/home/chexxor/Git/Durian-Pi`** — the seat that had been rooted at the approved
`durian-dev/seatroot` was served from **landed `main`**, and it created **`/home/chexxor/Git/Durian-Pi/item-4902`**, an
item worktree nested inside the delegate's own checkout (clean, no commits, invisible to `git status` because nested
worktrees are auto-ignored, visible to `git worktree list`).

**Why that is a durable decision and not just my mistake: the two roots have different *code*, so the seat got a
different registration.** `devtools` from landed `main`: `src/seattools.mjs` registers `shell: createPowerShellTool()`
unconditionally, `src/seatguard.mjs` still hardcodes `SHELL_TOOLS = new Set(["bash","powershell"])` (permission without
registration), and **`src/shellregistry.mjs` does not exist there** — its shell call returned **`spawn powershell
ENOENT`**. `impl` from `f8840349`: got `bash` and ran six commands at exit 0. Same rig, same minute, **two seats, two
registrations**. Every instrument reading "what the rig can do" is therefore only valid **for the tree it was read from**,
which is the same lesson D178 recorded for REDs, now demonstrated on a *capability*.

**Consequences the operator now has to rule on (the seat asked them directly in #4910):** which tree serves seats —
landed `Durian-Pi` (host-blind, no shell on Linux) or `durian-dev/seatroot @ f8840349` (has 217, which is not landed)?
Tonight's answer was accidental and differed per seat.

**The correct move, which I did not take, and why it stays un-taken.** Re-pointing 13 `pi.agent` records is a workspace
write with a documented history of destroying work
(`docs/incidents/2026-10-26-worktree-and-scratch-sweep.md`), and `up … --refresh --dry-run` printing `changes: {}` is
vacuous here (D178), so I had no trustworthy preview. Both drifted cwds sit on **clean** worktrees with **no uncommitted
work**, so nothing is at risk from leaving them; the risk is acting on them without an inventory. Next delegate: follow
`docs/runbooks/workspace-move.md` — inventory `git worktree list --porcelain`, `git branch --list`, `ls .spike | wc -l`
into `.spike/`, then one named verb, then diff the inventory.

**Routed, not fixed (all devtools-scope, none hand-patched by the delegate).** `#4915` (feature, held) — a fresh item
worktree is **not a comparable verification tree**: `prepare_workspace` itself printed `DEPENDENCY NOT LINKED … the
sync-pi --link step FAILED (vendor/pi-main is not built in this worktree … run --sync first)`, and the versions are

the landing-gate instruments don't read the registered shell: `channel-preflight` §7 scrapes the vendored PowerShell

**A new org-edge class defect surfaced while filing them: a seat cannot register a row to itself** (`org edge` refusal on

## D181 — the landing sequence can be executed *without* landing anything: the author's rebase with a patch-id gate, then the delegate moves the root, then everything stops at the merge; and a forgotten GPU slot spent three seat turns before one probe named it (delegate, 2026-10-31, Linux)

**The decision.** The operator agreed to a five-act sequence: `lead` mints/releases the rebase row → `impl` rebases with a
patch-id equivalence gate → the delegate moves the approved seat root to the rebased tip → an independent seat verifies on
a worktree forked from that tip → **stop at the merge/landing gate**. Acts 1–3 are done and verified; act 4 is blocked on a
host spend the operator holds; act 5 was never attempted. Nothing was merged, nothing pushed.

**Why the root move was the point, and why it was worth doing before the merge.** `seatroot/linux` was **15 commits behind
`main`**, which is not a cosmetic fact: `prepare_workspace` forks from the seat root, so **every worktree any seat created
was born 15 commits stale**, and that is exactly the condition that manufactured the fresh-worktree false REDs of D180
(#4915's `DEPENDENCY NOT LINKED`, the `schema version 2 > 1` failure, 80-vs-187 package counts). After the move the root is
**0 behind, 1 ahead**, so the staleness class is closed for every future wake — and #4905/#4906/#4917 were released by
`lead` in the same minute because the base stopped being a reason to hold them. **Fix divergence by landing, not by
re-rooting seats onto a tree that cannot run a seat shell** (landed `main` has no `src/shellregistry.mjs`; `devtools` there
got `spawn powershell ENOENT`).

**Why a patch-id, not a diff or an ancestry comparison, was the right pin.** A rebase changes the commit id and can change
the parent, while the *reviewed content* must not move. `git merge-tree --write-tree` (read-only) had already shown the
merge would be clean with all five 217 blobs byte-identical, so the pin made the rebase checkable in one boolean:
`279e0d9861b4d6958cf1f36af03dc00c96fcaa23` before and after. `impl` did it correctly — `git rebase main` (the two-argument
`--onto` form is refused by #4136's argument matching), exit 0, no conflict, tip `8a950542`, `main..HEAD` = 1,
`HEAD..main` = 0, parent count 1. **The delegate's role was deliberately the boring one:** rescue ref
(`refs/rescued/seatroot-linux-f8840349`), then `reset --hard`, with the workspace-move inventory taken as **refs, not only
directories** — `lead`'s sharpening, because the 2026-10-26 casualties were *branches* — and it paid for itself: **206
lines before, 206 after, exactly one changed line.**

**The discovery that changes how every "assert sha X" instruction must be written here: the redactor eats 40-hex tokens,
including the pinned patch-ids inside a row body.** `impl`'s geometry output and `lead`'s own pins came back as
`[redacted by durig: secret-shaped value (high-entropy-token)]`, i.e. the gate as written was **un-checkable**, and a seat
reporting "matched" against an unreadable pin would have been an unfalsifiable claim. `impl` kept it honest by computing
the comparison **inside the shell** and reporting a boolean plus two id halves. Routed as **#4922** (`security`): fix by
checker *class* (artifact-id vs credential), not by widening an allowlist, with the two-position demo as the non-vacuous
test.

**Three seat turns were spent before one probe named the blocker.** The verify leg died three times — `qa2` returned
`settledStatus:"done"` with **`stopReason:"length"`** and the reply `"I"`; `auditor` returned `unanswered`/`model_error`
twice. The reflex was to blame the seat (context band) and then the conversation shape; both were wrong. The cause was
measured in ~30 s: **LM Studio relaunched and restored `--ctx-size 8192 --parallel 4 --n-gpu-layers 27`** while both
gitignored `durig.config.json` files declare `DURIG_VERIFIER_CONTEXT = 24576`. Probing **at the size that fails** (not a
26-token probe) settles it: **6,128 tokens → `finish_reason=length`** (accepted, no room to answer), **9,128 → HTTP 400**,
**20,128 → HTTP 400** `exceeds the available context size (8192 tokens)`. This is `verifier-serving-headroom.md` Step 4's
recorded regression — "LM Studio forgets" — and it was re-encountered anyway because nothing in the wake path checks it.
**`raise-capacity-is-the-operator's-spend` held: the reload was costed (15,202 MiB at 24576×1 against 16,376, needing the
`Qwen3-VL-4B` 8192×4 slot unloaded) and not spent.** The zero-spend alternative is routing the verify leg to a
**local-model** seat (`security` 0.1367, `scribe` 0.1676) whose endpoint is healthy.

**A routing principle worth keeping: a fresh seat is the *more* independent verifier, not the less.** `lead` first chose
`qa2` over `qa` for "headroom plus independence"; the delegate's own brief destroyed the headroom premise (qa2 grew
18,842 → 20,192 of 24,576 = **0.8216**, statistically identical to qa's 0.8183), and `lead` cancelled its own row with its
error named in the reason. Independence is really **absence of anchoring** — a seat with `null` context (`auditor`) carries
no transcript of the debate about the change, so it cannot be talked into the author's conclusion. That argument is
stronger than the one for a peer who watched the whole thing.

**Two delegate errors, recorded because they are the repeatable kind.** (1) A **4.5 KB brief to a seat at 0.77 of a
24,576-token window** — the run never read a file. Brief size is a budget variable: the runbook's Step 5 already says
"cap the reading, put the cliff in the brief", and this rig's verifier seats have ~5.9k tokens of headroom at that band.
(2) **Backticks in a `printf`-written brief**: the shell ate `prepare_workspace(itemId: 4927)`, `main`, `item-4898`,
`refs/`, so the seat received a payload with its boundaries deleted — and the run errored. Write briefs with a file tool,
never through a shell command line. **And do not re-send a failed brief**: each attempt appends a user turn
(`Never re-send the same brief`, Step 1), so a retry is a deposit, not a repair.

**Anti-vacuity, from `lead`, worth restating.** After the rebase the portability audit went **2 findings → 1**
(`seat-shell-availability` gone; `seat-host-unaware` remaining). `lead` ruled the remainder **not 217's debt** — cut out
of #4849 at #4858 — and folded it into #4906 with the condition that the finding **stays named as outstanding**, because
"a clean audit after that change would be the suspicious result". A pass condition that *expects* a named outstanding
finding is the right shape for a gate that would otherwise be satisfied by deleting the evidence.

**Routed, not fixed (none of it hand-patched by the delegate).** **#4923** (`devtools`, urgent) — `rig-portability-audit`
prints **`seat roots read: 0`** while the store carries **13 resolving cwds** (`read-cwd4.mjs`, doc = conv+5, one orphan on
a dead `C:\` path); this breaks the denominator under `lead`'s own 2→0 gate, so any ruling that cites a count must cite a
verified reader. Same family: the audit printed **`model-slots: none loaded`** while two `llama-server` processes run.
**#4928** — **`done` + `stopReason:"length"` is a false green**; surface `stopReason` beside `settledStatus` and refuse at
`send` when the brief plus the seat's remaining window cannot fit (that arithmetic was computable *before* qa2 ran, and it
would have caught `lead`'s own row choice too); no new status word before measuring what the existing mapping pair
carries (#3112/#3021). **#4924** (held) — `> /dev/null` is refused as "a write outside your worktree": a discard is not a
write, and refusing it pushes seats into pipes, which is the false-green class this rig keeps meeting. **#4925**
(`architect`) — for `seat-host-unaware`, probe beats declaration: a declared host can be false, a probe cannot, so a
declaration is admissible only with a named consumer. **#4917** — **inline briefs**: `--file` is not a recognized flag, so
the seat received a *path* instead of a brief and refused to infer content from a filename.

### Clock-out notes — where the wall-clock went, and what would shorten it next time

- **Three dead provider wakes (~4–7 min each) cost more than the entire rebase.** The fix is a **pre-wake provider gate**,
  in this order and all three read-only: `seat-turn-shape` (seconds; the trap that cost four sessions), then
  `ps -eo args | grep -o -- "--ctx-size [0-9]*"` **compared against `DURIG_VERIFIER_CONTEXT` in `durig.config.json`**,
  then one probe **at the failing size**. Propose folding that second and third check into
  `tools/seat-turn-shape.mjs` as a capacity column — one instrument call instead of a session's worth of guessing. Routed
  as a finding, not built by the delegate.
- **`rows.mjs --context` is now load-bearing**: it prints census, requested rows, parked-on-`pm` rows, context fractions,
  and reachability from one 23 MB dump. `find.mjs` searches queue dumps for text the census cannot show. Both stayed in
  `.spike/fix-20261101/`.
- **Pointer-cap compression is again the largest clock-out line item** (199-line cap, verbatim archive cut). The
  `tools/pointer-fit.mjs` proposal from D178 stands: a checker that reports the pointer's line count and the first
  section boundary, so compression is measured before it is written by hand.
- **Wake yield, re-measured:** one `send` to `lead` (0.3555) with a ~2.4 KB brief closed and minted six rows in ~4 min;
  the same content to `pm` (0.9225, `model_error`) would have parked silently. **Batching briefs is worth far more on this
  rig than parallel wakes.**
